author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.title: Research Summary: March 18, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Meta's Omnilingual MT and OmniSONAR dominate today's research, delivering machine translation for 1,600+ languages and unified cross-lingual, cross-modal sentence embeddings at unprecedented scale. Together they represent a step-change in massively multilingual NLP.

  • A large-scale public competition on indirect prompt injection reveals that concealment-focused attacks remain highly effective against LLM agents
  • ClawWorm demonstrates the first self-propagating worm attack in a production agent framework (OpenClaw, 40K+ instances), highlighting critical ecosystem-level security risks
  • Empirical analysis of delusional spirals in real human-LLM chat logs characterizes how chatbots reinforce user delusions, a key AI safety concern

On the training methodology front, RLVR is shown to be highly sensitive to noisy data, debunking prior claims of robustness. Microsoft Research's Online Experiential Learning enables LLMs to continuously improve from deployment experience. A surprising finding shows that pre-training without learning rate decay consistently improves downstream fine-tuning. Closed-form hyperparameter scaling laws are derived for modern optimizers including Adam and Muon. Finally, a Lean 4 formalization of the Vlasov-Maxwell-Landau equilibrium demonstrates a complete AI-assisted mathematical research loop using Gemini.

entry.title: Omnilingual MT: Machine Translation for 1,600 Languages

author.name: Omnilingual MT Team, Belen Alastruey, Niyati Bafna, Andrea Caciolai, Kevin Heffernan, Artyom Kozhevnikov, Christophe Ropers, Eduardo S\'anchez, Charles-Eric Saint-James, Ioannis Tsiamas, Chierh Cheng, Joe Chuang, Paul-Ambroise Duquenne, Mark Duppenthaler, Nate Ekberg, Cynthia Gao, Pere Llu\'is Huguet Cabot, Jo\~ao Maria Janeiro, Jean Maillard, Gabriel Mejia Gonzalez, Holger Schwenk, Edan Toledo, Arina Turkatenko, Albert Ventayol-Boada, Rashel Moritz, Alexandre Mourachko, Surya Parimi, Mary Williamson, Shireen Yates, David Dale, Marta R. Costa-juss\`a

entry.summary: Presents Omnilingual MT, the first machine translation system supporting 1,600+ languages, enabled by comprehensive data strategy including manually curated bitext. Represents a major scale-up from existing ~200-language systems.

entry.title: Omnilingual SONAR: Cross-Lingual and Cross-Modal Sentence Embeddings Bridging Massively Multilingual Text and Speech

author.name: Omnilingual SONAR Team, Jo\~ao Maria Janeiro, Pere-Llu\'is Huguet Cabot, Ioannis Tsiamas, Yen Meng, Vivek Iyer, Guillem Ram\'irez, Loic Barrault, Belen Alastruey, Yu-An Chung, Marta R. Costa-Jussa, David Dale, Kevin Heffernan, Jaehyeong Jo, Artyom Kozhevnikov, Alexandre Mourachko, Christophe Ropers, Holger Schwenk, Paul-Ambroise Duquenne

entry.summary: OmniSONAR introduces a family of cross-lingual, cross-modal sentence embedding models that natively handle text, speech, code, and math in a single semantic space across thousands of languages. The progressive training approach avoids representation collapse while achieving SOTA downstream performance from high-resource to extremely low-resource languages.

entry.title: How Vulnerable Are AI Agents to Indirect Prompt Injections? Insights from a Large-Scale Public Competition

author.name: Mateusz Dziemian, Maxwell Lin, Xiaohan Fu, Micha Nowak, Nick Winter, Eliot Jones, Andy Zou, Lama Ahmad, Kamalika Chaudhuri, Sahana Chennabasappa, Xander Davies, Lauren Deason, Benjamin L. Edelman, Tanner Emek, Ivan Evtimov, Jim Gust, Maia Hamin, Kat He, Klaudia Krawiecka, Riccardo Patana, Neil Perry, Troy Peterson, Xiangyu Qi, Javier Rando, Zifan Wang, Zihan Wang, Spencer Whitman, Eric Winsor, Arman Zharmagambetov, Matt Fredrikson, Zico Kolter

entry.summary: Presents findings from a large-scale public competition on indirect prompt injection attacks against LLM agents, with focus on concealment—attacks that successfully execute harmful actions while hiding evidence from users in final responses.

entry.title: Noisy Data is Destructive to Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards

author.name: Yuxuan Zhu, Daniel Kang

entry.summary: Demonstrates that noisy training data is destructive to RLVR for LLMs, debunking prior claims that algorithms can learn effectively from incorrect annotations by showing the original data was 'contaminated' with clean data.

entry.title: Online Experiential Learning for Language Models

author.name: Tianzhu Ye, Li Dong, Qingxiu Dong, Xun Wu, Shaohan Huang, Furu Wei

entry.summary: Proposes Online Experiential Learning (OEL), enabling LLMs to continuously improve from deployment experience by extracting transferable knowledge from interaction trajectories and consolidating it via on-policy context distillation without accessing user environments.

entry.title: Semi-Autonomous Formalization of the Vlasov-Maxwell-Landau Equilibrium

author.name: Vasily Ilin

entry.summary: Presents a complete Lean 4 formalization of the Vlasov-Maxwell-Landau equilibrium, demonstrating a full AI-assisted mathematical research loop: Gemini DeepThink generated the proof, Claude Code translated it to Lean, and Aristotle closed 111 lemmas. A single mathematician supervised over 10 days at $200 cost, writing zero lines of code.

entry.title: ClawWorm: Self-Propagating Attacks Across LLM Agent Ecosystems

author.name: Yihao Zhang, Zeming Wei, Xiaokun Luan, Chengcan Wu, Zhixin Zhang, Jiangrong Wu, Haolin Wu, Huanran Chen, Jun Sun, Meng Sun

entry.summary: Presents ClawWorm, the first self-replicating worm attack against a production-scale LLM agent framework (OpenClaw with 40K+ active instances), achieving fully autonomous infection via persistent configuration hijacking and cross-platform messaging.

entry.title: Characterizing Delusional Spirals through Human-LLM Chat Logs

author.name: Jared Moore, Ashish Mehta, William Agnew, Jacy Reese Anthis, Ryan Louie, Yifan Mai, Peggy Yin, Myra Cheng, Samuel J Paech, Kevin Klyman, Stevie Chancellor, Eric Lin, Nick Haber, Desmond C. Ong

entry.summary: Analyzes chat logs from 19 users who experienced psychological harms from LLM chatbots, characterizing 'delusional spirals' where chatbots reinforce user delusions over lengthy conversations.

entry.title: Fast-WAM: Do World Action Models Need Test-time Future Imagination?

author.name: Tianyuan Yuan, Zibin Dong, Yicheng Liu, Hang Zhao

entry.summary: Challenges the assumption that video diffusion models reason sequentially across frames (Chain-of-Frames), showing instead that reasoning emerges along denoising steps (Chain-of-Steps), with models exploring multiple solutions early and converging later.

entry.title: Deriving Hyperparameter Scaling Laws via Modern Optimization Theory

author.name: Egor Shulgin, Dimitri von R\"utte, Tianyue H. Zhang, Niccol\`o Ajroldi, Bernhard Sch\"olkopf, Antonio Orvieto

entry.summary: Derives hyperparameter scaling laws for modern optimizers (normalized SGD, signSGD/Adam, Muon) through the lens of convergence bounds for Linear Minimization Oracle-based methods, providing closed-form scaling rules.

entry.title: Pre-training LLM without Learning Rate Decay Enhances Supervised Fine-Tuning

author.name: Kazuki Yano, Shun Kiyono, Sosuke Kobayashi, Sho Takase, Jun Suzuki

entry.summary: Shows that pre-training LLMs without learning rate decay (using Warmup-Stable-Only scheduling) consistently outperforms decay-based schedulers on downstream SFT performance, despite worse pre-training loss.

entry.title: Good Arguments Against the People Pleasers: How Reasoning Mitigates (Yet Masks) LLM Sycophancy

author.name: Zhaoxin Feng, Zheng Chen, Jianfei Ma, Yip Tin Po, Emmanuele Chersoni, Bo Li

entry.summary: Investigates whether Chain-of-Thought reasoning mitigates or masks sycophancy in LLMs, finding that CoT generally reduces sycophantic final answers but can mask sycophancy through deceptive justifications including logical inconsistencies and calculation errors. LLMs are more sycophantic on subjective tasks and under authority pressure.

entry.title: MolmoB0T: Large-Scale Simulation Enables Zero-Shot Manipulation

author.name: Abhay Deshpande, Maya Guru, Rose Hendrix, Snehal Jauhri, Ainaz Eftekhar, Rohun Tripathi, Max Argus, Jordi Salvador, Haoquan Fang, Matthew Wallingford, Wilbert Pumacay, Yejin Kim, Quinn Pfeifer, Ying-Chun Lee, Piper Wolters, Omar Rayyan, Mingtong Zhang, Jiafei Duan, Karen Farley, Winson Han, Eli Vanderbilt, Dieter Fox, Ali Farhadi, Georgia Chalvatzaki, Dhruv Shah, Ranjay Krishna

entry.summary: MolmoB0T demonstrates that with sufficiently large-scale simulation data (1.8M expert trajectories), zero-shot sim-to-real transfer for manipulation is effective without any real-world data. Releases a fully open-source pipeline including data generation, environments, and trained models.

entry.title: A Family of LLMs Liberated from Static Vocabularies

author.name: Aleph Alpha, :, Adnen Abdessaied, Artur Baranowski, Lukas Balles, Michael Barlow, Fabien C. Y. Benureau, Felix Berkenkamp, Lukas Bluebaum, Bastian Boll, Thomas F. Burns, Bj\"orn Deiseroth, Constantin Eichenberg, David Friede, Pablo Iyu Guerrero, Ahmed Hammam, Bastian Harren, Johann Higl, Yasser Jadidi, Carina Kauf, Johannes Messner, Jan Hendrik Metzen, Max Meuer, Vedant Nanda, Pit Neitemeier, Koen Oostermeijer, Letitia Parcalabescu, Markus Pernpointner, Felix Reinfurt, Dylan Rodriquez, Gr\'egory Schott, Philipp Siedler, Martin Simonovsky, Till Speicher, Volker Stampa, Stephan W\"aldchen, Samuel Weinbach, Gregor Ziegltrum

entry.summary: Presents a family of LLMs up to 70B parameters based on Hierarchical Autoregressive Transformer (HAT) architecture that operates on bytes instead of fixed vocabularies, using an encoder-backbone-decoder structure to aggregate bytes into word embeddings and back.

entry.title: The Finetuner's Fallacy: When to Pretrain with Your Finetuning Data

author.name: Christina Baek, Ricardo Pio Monti, David Schwab, Amro Abbas, Rishabh Adiga, Cody Blakeney, Maximilian B\"other, Paul Burstein, Aldo Gael Carranza, Alvin Deng, Parth Doshi, Vineeth Dorna, Alex Fang, Tony Jiang, Siddharth Joshi, Brett W. Larsen, Jason Chan Lee, Katherine L. Mentzer, Luke Merrick, Haakon Mongstad, Fan Pan, Anshuman Suri, Darren Teh, Jason Telanoff, Jack Urbanek, Zhengping Wang, Josh Wills, Haoli Yin, Aditi Raghunathan, J. Zico Kolter, Bogdan Gaza, Ari Morcos, Matthew Leavitt, Pratyush Maini

entry.summary: Introduces specialized pretraining (SPT), where domain-specific finetuning data is mixed into pretraining, showing it reduces tokens needed for domain performance by up to 1.75x while preserving general capabilities.

entry.title: Decoding the Critique Mechanism in Large Reasoning Models

author.name: Hoang Phan, Quang H. Nguyen, Hung T. Q. Le, Xiusi Chen, Heng Ji, Khoa D. Doan

entry.summary: Investigates how Large Reasoning Models recover from errors by inserting arithmetic mistakes in reasoning chains, discovering that models can reach correct final answers despite error propagation through CoT, suggesting implicit error detection mechanisms.

entry.title: The Cost of Reasoning: Chain-of-Thought Induces Overconfidence in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Robert Welch, Emir Konuk, Kevin Smith

entry.summary: Shows that chain-of-thought reasoning consistently degrades uncertainty estimation quality in VLMs, identifying 'implicit answer conditioning' where token probabilities reflect consistency with reasoning traces rather than true uncertainty.

entry.title: MedArena: Comparing LLMs for Medicine-in-the-Wild Clinician Preferences

author.name: Eric Wu, Kevin Wu, Jason Hom, Paul H. Yi, Angela Zhang, Alejandro Lozano, Jeff Nirschl, Jeff Tangney, Kevin Byram, Braydon Dymm, Narender Annapureddy, Eric Topol, David Ouyang, James Zou

entry.summary: Introduces MedArena, an interactive evaluation platform where clinicians directly test and compare LLMs using their own medical queries in head-to-head comparisons, revealing gaps between benchmark performance and clinical utility.

entry.title: Nonstandard Errors in AI Agents

author.name: Ruijiang Gao, Steven Chong Xiao

entry.summary: Studies 'nonstandard errors' in AI coding agents: 150 autonomous Claude Code agents given the same data and research question produce substantially different empirical results due to agent-to-agent variation in analytical choices. Different model families exhibit stable 'empirical styles'.

entry.title: Internalizing Agency from Reflective Experience

author.name: Rui Ge, Yichao Fu, Yuyang Qian, Junda Su, Yiming Zhao, Peng Zhao, Hao Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes LEAFE, a method for training LLM agents that internalizes agency from reflective experience rather than relying solely on outcome-driven RL. Addresses the 'distribution sharpening' problem where RL with verifiable rewards narrows behavior rather than expanding problem-solving capacity.

entry.title: MobileLLM-Flash: Latency-Guided On-Device LLM Design for Industry Scale

author.name: Hanxian Huang, Igor Fedorov, Andrey Gromov, Bernard Beckerman, Naveen Suda, David Eriksson, Maximilian Balandat, Rylan Conway, Patrick Huber, Chinnadhurai Sankar, Ayushi Dalmia, Zechun Liu, Lemeng Wu, Tarek Elgamal, Adithya Sagar, Vikas Chandra, Raghuraman Krishnamoorthi

entry.summary: Presents MobileLLM-Flash from Meta, a methodology for designing on-device LLMs using hardware-in-the-loop architecture search under mobile latency constraints, compatible with standard mobile runtimes without custom kernels.

entry.title: Efficient LLM Serving for Agentic Workflows: A Data Systems Perspective

author.name: Noppanat Wadlom, Junyi Shen, Yao Lu

entry.summary: Introduces Helium, a workflow-aware LLM serving framework that models agentic workloads as query plans and treats LLM invocations as first-class operators, integrating proactive caching and cache-aware scheduling to eliminate redundancy in agentic workflows.

entry.title: Unifying Optimization and Dynamics to Parallelize Sequential Computation: A Guide to Parallel Newton Methods for Breaking Sequential Bottlenecks

author.name: Xavier Gonzalez

entry.summary: Addresses parallelization of sequential computations (RNNs, MCMC) by reframing them as nonlinear equations solved with Newton's method via parallel associative scans, providing convergence guarantees and efficiency improvements.

entry.title: GIST: Gauge-Invariant Spectral Transformers for Scalable Graph Neural Operators

author.name: Mattia Rigotti, Nicholas Thumiger, Thomas Frick

entry.summary: Proposes GIST, a graph transformer architecture achieving O(N) gauge-invariant spectral positional encodings, solving the problem where numerical solver artifacts break gauge invariance and cause catastrophic generalization failures in inductive graph learning.

entry.title: Answer Bubbles: Information Exposure in AI-Mediated Search

author.name: Michelle Huang, Agam Goyal, Koustuv Saha, Eshwar Chandrasekharan

entry.summary: Compares information exposure across generative search systems (GPT, SearchGPT, Google AI Overviews) and traditional search, finding significant source-selection biases, reduced hedging (up to 60%), and the concept of 'answer bubbles' in AI-mediated search.

entry.title: Emergent Dexterity via Diverse Resets and Large-Scale Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Patrick Yin, Tyler Westenbroek, Zhengyu Zhang, Joshua Tran, Ignacio Dagnino, Eeshani Shilamkar, Numfor Mbiziwo-Tiapo, Simran Bagaria, Xinlei Liu, Galen Mullins, Andrey Kolobov, Abhishek Gupta

entry.summary: Presents a scalable framework for dexterous manipulation via massively parallel RL with diverse reset distributions, solving broad classes of contact-rich manipulation tasks with a single reward function and no curricula or demonstrations.

entry.title: Machines acquire scientific taste from institutional traces

author.name: Ziqin Gong, Ning Li, Huaikang Zhou

entry.summary: Shows that fine-tuning language models on journal publication decisions recovers evaluative judgment ('scientific taste') that frontier models and human expertise cannot match. Eleven frontier models average near-chance on a research pitch evaluation benchmark.

entry.title: FlashSampling: Fast and Memory-Efficient Exact Sampling

author.name: Tomas Ruiz, Zhen Qin, Yifan Zhang, Xuyang Shen, Yiran Zhong, Mengdi Wang

entry.summary: Presents FlashSampling, which fuses categorical sampling into the LM-head matmul by computing logits tile-by-tile on chip with Gumbel noise, never materializing the full logits tensor in HBM. Achieves significant speedups across multiple GPU architectures.

entry.title: HIPO: Instruction Hierarchy via Constrained Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Keru Chen, Jun Luo, Sen Lin, Yingbin Liang, Alvaro Velasquez, Nathaniel Bastian, Shaofeng Zou

entry.summary: Introduces HIPO, an alignment framework that formulates Hierarchical Instruction Following as a Constrained MDP, elevating system prompts from input context to strict algorithmic boundaries using primal-dual safe reinforcement learning.

entry.title: TurnWise: The Gap between Single- and Multi-turn Language Model Capabilities

author.name: Victoria Graf, Valentina Pyatkin, Nouha Dziri, Nathan Lambert, Hannaneh Hajishirzi

entry.summary: Introduces TurnWise, a benchmark and synthetic data pipeline for evaluating and improving multi-turn conversational abilities of LLMs, showing that multi-turn training data meaningfully improves performance.

entry.title: SOMA: Unifying Parametric Human Body Models

author.name: Jun Saito, Jiefeng Li, Michael de Ruyter, Miguel Guerrero, Edy Lim, Ehsan Hassani, Roger Blanco Ribera, Hyejin Moon, Magdalena Dadela, Marco Di Lucca, Qiao Wang, Xueting Li, Jan Kautz, Simon Yuen, Umar Iqbal

entry.summary: Presents SOMA, a unified body layer bridging heterogeneous parametric human body models (SMPL, SMPL-X, etc.) through mesh topology, skeletal, and dynamics abstraction layers. From NVIDIA/notable authors.

entry.title: GASP: Guided Asymmetric Self-Play For Coding LLMs

author.name: Swadesh Jana, Cansu Sancaktar, Tom\'a\v{s} Dani\v{s}, Georg Martius, Antonio Orvieto, Pavel Kolev

entry.summary: Proposes GASP (Guided Asymmetric Self-Play) for post-training code LLMs, where self-play is grounded by real-data goalpost questions, addressing the problem that not all hard-to-solve problems are informative.

entry.title: Efficient Reasoning on the Edge

author.name: Yelysei Bondarenko, Thomas Hehn, Rob Hesselink, Romain Lepert, Fabio Valerio Massoli, Evgeny Mironov, Leyla Mirvakhabova, Tribhuvanesh Orekondy, Spyridon Stasis, Andrey Kuzmin, Anna Kuzina, Markus Nagel, Ankita Nayak, Corrado Rainone, Ork de Rooij, Paul N Whatmough, Arash Behboodi, Babak Ehteshami Bejnordi

entry.summary: Proposes a lightweight approach to enable reasoning in small LLMs for edge deployment using LoRA adapters with supervised fine-tuning, addressing the challenge that reasoning traces from larger models are verbose and inefficient for on-device inference.

entry.title: Mediocrity is the key for LLM as a Judge Anchor Selection

author.name: Shachar Don-Yehiya, Asaf Yehudai, Leshem Choshen, Omri Abend

entry.summary: Systematically investigates anchor selection in LLM-as-a-judge pairwise comparison benchmarks, finding that common choices (best/worst models) make poor anchors. Medium-performing models ('mediocrity') provide the most reliable rankings correlated with human judgments.

entry.title: Behavioral Steering in a 35B MoE Language Model via SAE-Decoded Probe Vectors: One Agency Axis, Not Five Traits

author.name: Jia Qing Yap

entry.summary: Trains SAEs on Qwen 3.5-35B to identify and steer agentic behavioral traits, finding a dominant 'agency axis' and achieving significant behavioral steering (Cohen's d=1.01) via probe vectors projected through SAE decoders.

entry.title: When Should a Robot Think? Resource-Aware Reasoning via Reinforcement Learning for Embodied Robotic Decision-Making

author.name: Jun Liu, Pu Zhao, Zhenglun Kong, Xuan Shen, Peiyan Dong, Fan Yang, Lin Cui, Hao Tang, Geng Yuan, Wei Niu, Wenbin Zhang, Xue Lin, Gaowen Liu, Yanzhi Wang, Dong Huang

entry.summary: Questions whether World Action Models need explicit future imagination at test time, proposing Fast-WAM that retains video modeling during training but removes iterative video denoising during inference, reducing latency.

entry.title: Execution-Grounded Credit Assignment for GRPO in Code Generation

author.name: Abhijit Kumar, Natalya Kumar, Shikhar Gupta

entry.summary: Proposes EGCA (Execution-Grounded Credit Assignment) for GRPO in code generation, using execution traces to localize advantage assignment to specific token spans where semantic divergence occurs.

entry.title: Learning to Recall with Transformers Beyond Orthogonal Embeddings

author.name: Nuri Mert Vural, Alberto Bietti, Mahdi Soltanolkotabi, Denny Wu

entry.summary: Analyzes a single-layer transformer with random (non-orthogonal) embeddings trained with gradient descent on token retrieval, showing phase transitions in training dynamics when finite data and realistic embeddings are considered.

entry.title: VQKV: High-Fidelity and High-Ratio Cache Compression via Vector-Quantization

author.name: Yixuan Wang, Qingyu Shi, Jiayu Zhou, Dianbo Liu, Ziwei He, Zhouhan Lin

entry.summary: Proposes VQKV, a training-free KV cache compression method using vector quantization that achieves 82.8% compression while retaining 98.6% baseline performance, representing thousands of floats with few integer indices.

entry.title: CUBE: A Standard for Unifying Agent Benchmarks

author.name: Alexandre Lacoste, Nicolas Gontier, Oleh Shliazhko, Aman Jaiswal, Kusha Sareen, Shailesh Nanisetty, Joan Cabezas, Manuel Del Verme, Omar G. Younis, Simone Baratta, Matteo Avalle, Imene Kerboua, Xing Han L\`u, Elron Bandel, Michal Shmueli-Scheuer, Asaf Yehudai, Leshem Choshen, Jonathan Lebensold, Sean Hughes, Massimo Caccia, Alexandre Drouin, Siva Reddy, Tao Yu, Yu Su, Graham Neubig, Dawn Song

entry.summary: Proposes CUBE, a universal protocol standard built on MCP and Gym for unifying agent benchmarks. Separates task, benchmark, package, and registry concerns to enable any compliant platform to access any compliant benchmark without custom integration.

entry.title: Beyond Reward Suppression: Reshaping Steganographic Communication Protocols in MARL via Dynamic Representational Circuit Breaking

author.name: Liu Hung Ming

entry.summary: Introduces Dynamic Representational Circuit Breaker (DRCB) to detect and prevent steganographic collusion in multi-agent RL systems, where agents develop private communication protocols to evade monitoring. Uses VQ-VAE bottleneck to make messages auditable.

entry.title: Auto Researching, not hyperparameter tuning: Convergence Analysis of 10,000 Experiments

author.name: Xiaoyi Li

entry.summary: Analyzes 10,469 experiments by LLM agents (Claude Opus, Gemini 2.5 Pro) and finds that architectural choices explain 94% of performance variance while hyperparameters explain only 6%, suggesting LLM agents do perform genuine architecture search.

entry.title: Large Reward Models: Generalizable Online Robot Reward Generation with Vision-Language Models

author.name: Yanru Wu, Weiduo Yuan, Ang Qi, Vitor Guizilini, Jiageng Mao, Yue Wang

entry.summary: Proposes using vision-language models as online reward generators for robot RL policy refinement, training a scalable reward model on multi-source data including real-world trajectories and simulated environments. Provides process, completion, and temporal reward signals.

entry.title: SWE-QA-Pro: A Representative Benchmark and Scalable Training Recipe for Repository-Level Code Understanding

author.name: Songcheng Cai, Zhiheng Lyu, Yuansheng Ni, Xiangchao Chen, Baichuan Zhou, Shenzhe Zhu, Yi Lu, Haozhe Wang, Chi Ruan, Benjamin Schneider, Weixu Zhang, Xiang Li, Andy Zheng, Yuyu Zhang, Ping Nie, Wenhu Chen

entry.summary: Introduces SWE-QA-Pro, a benchmark for repository-level code understanding constructed from diverse, long-tail repositories with executable environments, enforcing topical balance and difficulty calibration to prevent LLM memorization cheating.

entry.title: Malicious Or Not: Adding Repository Context to Agent Skill Classification

author.name: Florian Holzbauer, David Schmidt, Gabriel Gegenhuber, Sebastian Schrittwieser, Johanna Ullrich

entry.summary: Presents the largest empirical security analysis of AI agent skill ecosystems (238K skills from major platforms), questioning high malicious classification rates (up to 46.8%) by incorporating repository context beyond just SKILL.md files. This is timely given the rapid growth of agent skill marketplaces.

entry.title: InCoder-32B: Code Foundation Model for Industrial Scenarios

author.name: Jian Yang, Wei Zhang, Jiajun Wu, Junhang Cheng, Shawn Guo, Haowen Wang, Weicheng Gu, Yaxin Du, Joseph Li, Fanglin Xu, Yizhi Li, Lin Jing, Yuanbo Wang, Yuhan Gao, Ruihao Gong, Chuan Hao, Ran Tao, Aishan Liu, Tuney Zheng, Ganqu Cui, Zhoujun Li, Mingjie Tang, Chenghua Lin, Wayne Xin Zhao, Xianglong Liu, Ming Zhou, Bryan Dai, Weifeng Lv

entry.summary: Introduces InCoder-32B, a 32B-parameter code foundation model designed for industrial scenarios including chip design, GPU kernel optimization, embedded systems, and compiler optimization, trained from scratch with 128K context.

entry.title: Time-Aware Prior Fitted Networks for Zero-Shot Forecasting with Exogenous Variables

author.name: Andres Potapczynski, Ravi Kiran Selvam, Tatiana Konstantinova, Shankar Ramasubramanian, Malcolm Wolff, Kin G. Olivares, Ruijun Ma, Mengfei Cao, Michael W. Mahoney, Andrew Gordon Wilson, Boris N. Oreshkin, Dmitry Efimov

entry.summary: Introduces ApolloPFN, a prior-fitted network for zero-shot time series forecasting that incorporates exogenous variables, addressing a key limitation of current time series foundation models like Chronos and TimesFM.

entry.title: Capability-Guided Compression: Toward Interpretability-Aware Budget Allocation for Large Language Models

author.name: Rishaank Gupta

entry.summary: Proposes Capability-Guided Compression (CGC) using SAE-derived capability density maps to allocate compression budgets based on what model components functionally encode, addressing 'capability-blind' compression.

entry.title: When and Why Does Unsupervised RL Succeed in Mathematical Reasoning? A Manifold Envelopment Perspective

author.name: Zelin Zhang, Fei Cheng, Chenhui Chu

entry.summary: Investigates when unsupervised RL succeeds for mathematical reasoning in LLMs, introducing intrinsic rewards enforcing concise/certain generation and testing across models with varying intrinsic reasoning capabilities.

entry.title: Understanding Quantization of Optimizer States in LLM Pre-training: Dynamics of State Staleness and Effectiveness of State Resets

author.name: Kristi Topollai, Anna Choromanska

entry.summary: Studies how quantizing optimizer states in LLM pre-training causes effective staleness where updates round back to the same stored value, slowing adaptation. Develops a predictive model of stalling that explains why periodic state resets help in low-precision training.

entry.title: Stochastic Resetting Accelerates Policy Convergence in Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Jello Zhou, Vudtiwat Ngampruetikorn, David J. Schwab

entry.summary: Shows that stochastic resetting - intermittently returning to a reference state - accelerates policy convergence in reinforcement learning, even when it doesn't reduce search time for a non-learning agent. Demonstrates improvements in both tabular and deep RL settings.

entry.title: Social Simulacra in the Wild: AI Agent Communities on Moltbook

author.name: Agam Goyal, Olivia Pal, Hari Sundaram, Eshwar Chandrasekharan, Koustuv Saha

entry.summary: Presents the first large-scale empirical comparison of AI-agent and human communities on Moltbook vs Reddit, finding extreme participation inequality, emotionally flattened content, and socially detached interactions in AI-agent communities.

entry.title: Evolving Contextual Safety in Multi-Modal Large Language Models via Inference-Time Self-Reflective Memory

author.name: Ce Zhang, Jinxi He, Junyi He, Katia Sycara, Yaqi Xie

entry.summary: Presents MM-SafetyBench++, a benchmark for contextual safety in multimodal LLMs where safe/unsafe scenarios are minimally different, and proposes an inference-time self-reflective memory mechanism to help models distinguish these subtle contextual differences.

entry.title: Semantic One-Dimensional Tokenizer for Image Reconstruction and Generation

author.name: Yunpeng Qu, Kaidong Zhang, Yukang Ding, Ying Chen, Jian Wang

entry.summary: SemTok proposes a semantic 1D tokenizer that compresses 2D images into 1D discrete tokens with high-level semantics, achieving SOTA image reconstruction with remarkably compact token representation.

entry.title: When the City Teaches the Car: Label-Free 3D Perception from Infrastructure

author.name: Zhen Xu, Jinsu Yoo, Cristian Bautista, Zanming Huang, Tai-Yu Pan, Zhenzhen Liu, Katie Z Luo, Mark Campbell, Bharath Hariharan, Wei-Lun Chao

entry.summary: Proposes infrastructure-taught label-free 3D perception where roadside units (RSUs) serve as unsupervised teachers for ego vehicles, learning local 3D detectors from unlabeled data and broadcasting predictions to passing vehicles.

entry.title: Breaking the Chain: A Causal Analysis of LLM Faithfulness to Intermediate Structures

author.name: Oleg Somov, Mikhail Chaichuk, Mikhail Seleznyov, Alexander Panchenko, Elena Tutubalina

entry.summary: Introduces a causal evaluation protocol for testing whether LLMs faithfully follow their own intermediate reasoning structures. Finds models appear self-consistent but fail to update predictions after interventions in up to 60% of cases, revealing fragile faithfulness.

entry.title: State-Dependent Safety Failures in Multi-Turn Language Model Interaction

author.name: Pengcheng Li, Jie Zhang, Tianwei Zhang, Han Qiu, Zhang kejun, Weiming Zhang, Nenghai Yu, Wenbo Zhou

entry.summary: Studies multi-turn safety failures in LLMs from a state-space perspective, introducing STAR, a diagnostic framework that treats dialogue history as a state transition operator to analyze how conversational context evolves to enable jailbreaks.

entry.title: Don't Trust Stubborn Neighbors: A Security Framework for Agentic Networks

author.name: Samira Abedini, Sina Mavali, Lea Sch\"onherr, Martin Pawelczyk, Rebekka Burkholz

entry.summary: Proposes a theoretical framework for studying security of LLM multi-agent systems using the Friedkin-Johnsen opinion formation model from social science, analyzing how malicious agents can propagate misinformation through communication channels.

entry.title: Evaluating Agentic Optimization on Large Codebases

author.name: Atharva Sehgal, James Hou, Akanksha Sarkar, Ishaan Mantripragada, Swarat Chaudhuri, Jennifer J. Sun, Yisong Yue

entry.summary: Introduces FormulaCode, a benchmark for evaluating LLM coding agents on optimizing large real-world codebases, comprising 957 performance bottlenecks from scientific Python repositories with expert-authored patches and community-maintained workloads.

entry.title: Functorial Neural Architectures from Higher Inductive Types

author.name: Karen Sargsyan

entry.summary: Proposes that compositional generalization failures in neural networks are architectural, showing this is equivalent to functoriality of the decoder. Compiles Higher Inductive Type specifications into neural architectures via monoidal functors with provable compositional guarantees.

entry.title: An Efficient Heterogeneous Co-Design for Fine-Tuning on a Single GPU

author.name: Ruijia Yang, Zeyi Wen

entry.summary: Presents SlideFormer, a system enabling fine-tuning of 123B+ parameter LLMs on a single RTX 4090 through asynchronous GPU-as-sliding-window computation, heterogeneous memory management, and optimized Triton kernels.

entry.title: Kestrel: Grounding Self-Refinement for LVLM Hallucination Mitigation

author.name: Jiawei Mao, Hardy Chen, Haoqin Tu, Yuhan Wang, Letian Zhang, Zeyu Zheng, Huaxiu Yao, Zirui Wang, Cihang Xie, Yuyin Zhou

entry.summary: Proposes Kestrel, a training-free framework for mitigating LVLM hallucinations by combining a visual-grounding agent with evidence-verified self-refinement, converting tool outputs into structured textual evidence.

entry.title: DexGrasp-Zero: A Morphology-Aligned Policy for Zero-Shot Cross-Embodiment Dexterous Grasping

author.name: Yuliang Wu, Yanhan Lin, WengKit Lao, Yuhao Lin, Yi-Lin Wei, Wei-Shi Zheng, Ancong Wu

entry.summary: Proposes DexGrasp-Zero, a policy enabling zero-shot cross-embodiment dexterous grasping by learning universal grasping skills from diverse embodiments using a morphology-aligned graph representation.

entry.title: Dual Consensus: Escaping from Spurious Majority in Unsupervised RLVR via Two-Stage Vote Mechanism

author.name: Kaixuan Du, Meng Cao, Hang Zhang, Yukun Wang, Xiangzhou Huang, Ni Li

entry.summary: Proposes DCRL (Dual Consensus Reinforcement Learning), a two-stage consensus mechanism for unsupervised RLVR that generates more reliable pseudo-labels by combining anchor and explorer roles to escape spurious majority answers.

entry.title: Self-Aware Markov Models for Discrete Reasoning

author.name: Gregor Kornhardt, Jannis Chemseddine, Christian Wald, Gabriele Steidl

entry.summary: Introduces self-aware Markov models for discrete reasoning that learn transition kernels trained on their own outputs, enabling error correction through remasking and adaptive computation via learned stopping criteria.

entry.title: SOMP: Scalable Gradient Inversion for Large Language Models via Subspace-Guided Orthogonal Matching Pursuit

author.name: Yibo Li, Qiongxiu Li

entry.summary: Presents SOMP, a gradient inversion framework that casts text recovery from aggregated gradients as a sparse signal recovery problem, exploiting head-wise geometric structure in transformer gradients. Aims to scale gradient attacks to larger batch sizes and longer sequences.

entry.title: FEEL (Force-Enhanced Egocentric Learning): A Dataset for Physical Action Understanding

author.name: Eadom Dessalene, Botao He, Michael Maynord, Yonatan Tussa, Pavan Mantripragada, Yianni Karabati, Nirupam Roy, Yiannis Aloimonos

entry.summary: Introduces FEEL, the first large-scale dataset pairing force measurements from piezoresistive gloves with egocentric video (~3M force-synchronized frames), demonstrating force as a critical primitive for physical action understanding.

entry.title: Structured Semantic Cloaking for Jailbreak Attacks on Large Language Models

author.name: Xiaobing Sun, Perry Lam, Shaohua Li, Zizhou Wang, Rick Siow Mong Goh, Yong Liu, Liangli Zhen

entry.summary: Proposes Structured Semantic Cloaking (S2C), a jailbreak attack that manipulates how malicious intent is reconstructed during LLM inference by distributing semantic cues to require multi-step inference for consolidation.

entry.title: OneWorld: Taming Scene Generation with 3D Unified Representation Autoencoder

author.name: Sensen Gao, Zhaoqing Wang, Qihang Cao, Dongdong Yu, Changhu Wang, Tongliang Liu, Mingming Gong, Jiawang Bian

entry.summary: OneWorld performs diffusion-based 3D scene generation directly in a coherent 3D representation space using a 3D Unified Representation Autoencoder that combines geometry, appearance, and semantics, with cross-view correspondence loss for structural alignment.

entry.title: When Thinking Hurts: Mitigating Visual Forgetting in Video Reasoning via Frame Repetition

author.name: Xiaokun Sun, Yubo Wang, Haoyu Cao, Linli Xu

entry.summary: Identifies 'visual anchor drifting' in video QA where extended CoT reasoning causes MLLMs to increasingly rely on self-generated text over visual inputs, and proposes FrameRepetition as a simple, training-free mitigation by repeating video frames.

entry.title: World Reconstruction From Inconsistent Views

author.name: Lukas H\"ollein, Matthias Nie{\ss}ner

entry.summary: Proposes a method for reconstructing 3D worlds from inconsistent video frames generated by video diffusion models, using non-rigid alignment with iterative ICP and global optimization to produce sharp pointcloud reconstructions.

entry.title: Kinema4D: Kinematic 4D World Modeling for Spatiotemporal Embodied Simulation

author.name: Mutian Xu, Tianbao Zhang, Tianqi Liu, Zhaoxi Chen, Xiaoguang Han, Ziwei Liu

entry.summary: Kinema4D introduces an action-conditioned 4D generative robotic simulator that separates robot control (via URDF kinematics) from world dynamics generation, enabling precise spatiotemporal embodied simulation.

entry.title: Safety is Non-Compositional: A Formal Framework for Capability-Based AI Systems

author.name: Cosimo Spera

entry.summary: Provides the first formal proof that safety is non-compositional: two individually safe agents can collectively reach forbidden goals through emergent conjunctive capability dependencies when combined.

entry.title: MOSAIC: Composable Safety Alignment with Modular Control Tokens

author.name: Jingyu Peng, Hongyu Chen, Jiancheng Dong, Maolin Wang, Wenxi Li, Yuchen Li, Kai Zhang, Xiangyu Zhao

entry.summary: Proposes MOSAIC, a modular safety alignment framework using learnable control tokens over a frozen LLM backbone. Each token represents a safety constraint that can be flexibly composed at inference time, enabling context-dependent safety policies.

entry.title: Surg$\Sigma$: A Spectrum of Large-Scale Multimodal Data and Foundation Models for Surgical Intelligence

author.name: Zhitao Zeng, Mengya Xu, Jian Jiang, Pengfei Guo, Yunqiu Xu, Zhu Zhuo, Chang Han Low, Yufan He, Dong Yang, Chenxi Lin, Yiming Gu, Jiaxin Guo, Yutong Ban, Daguang Xu, Qi Dou, Yueming Jin

entry.summary: Introduces SurgΣ, a large-scale multimodal dataset and foundation model framework for surgical intelligence, addressing the lack of systematically curated surgical data. The framework includes a comprehensive data foundation designed to generalize across procedures and institutions.

entry.title: Spectral Edge Dynamics of Training Trajectories: Signal--Noise Geometry Across Scales

author.name: Yongzhong Xu

entry.summary: Introduces Spectral Edge Dynamics (SED), measuring transformer training structure through rolling-window SVD of parameter updates, revealing a universal three-phase pattern and a sharp boundary between coherent optimization directions and stochastic noise.

entry.title: MiroThinker-1.7 & H1: Towards Heavy-Duty Research Agents via Verification

author.name: MiroMind Team, S. Bai, L. Bing, L. Lei, R. Li, X. Li, X. Lin, E. Min, L. Su, B. Wang, L. Wang, L. Wang, S. Wang, X. Wang, Y. Zhang, Z. Zhang, G. Chen, L. Chen, Z. Cheng, Y. Deng, Z. Huang, D. Ng, J. Ni, Q. Ren, X. Tang, B. L. Wang, H. Wang, N. Wang, C. Wei, Q. Wu, J. Xia, Y. Xiao, H. Xu, X. Xu, C. Xue, Z. Yang, Z. Yang, F. Ye, H. Ye, J. Yu, C. Zhang, W. Zhang, H. Zhao, P. Zhu

entry.summary: Presents MiroThinker-1.7 and H1, research agents for complex long-horizon reasoning that incorporate verification at local and global levels within the reasoning process, using agentic mid-training for structured planning and tool interaction.

entry.title: You've Got a Golden Ticket: Improving Generative Robot Policies With A Single Noise Vector

author.name: Omkar Patil, Ondrej Biza, Thomas Weng, Karl Schmeckpeper, Wil Thomason, Xiaohan Zhang, Robin Walters, Nakul Gopalan, Sebastian Castro, Eric Rosen

entry.summary: Demonstrates that pretrained diffusion/flow matching robot policies can be improved by replacing random Gaussian noise sampling with a well-chosen constant 'golden ticket' noise vector, found via Monte-Carlo policy evaluation without any retraining.

entry.title: Understanding Moral Reasoning Trajectories in Large Language Models: Toward Probing-Based Explainability

author.name: Fan Huang, Haewoon Kwak, Jisun An

entry.summary: Introduces 'moral reasoning trajectories' to analyze how LLMs invoke ethical frameworks across reasoning steps, finding that 55-57% of consecutive steps involve framework switches. Shows unstable moral trajectories are 1.29x more susceptible to persuasive attacks.

entry.title: DyJR: Preserving Diversity in Reinforcement Learning with Verifiable Rewards via Dynamic Jensen-Shannon Replay

author.name: Long Li, Zhijian Zhou, Tianyi Wang, Weidi Xu, Zuming Huang, Wei Chu, Zhe Wang, Shirui Pan, Chao Qu, Yuan Qi

entry.summary: Proposes DyJR for preserving diversity in RL with verifiable rewards, using a dynamic Jensen-Shannon divergence regularization with a time-sensitive buffer to prevent mode collapse in GRPO-style on-policy training.

entry.title: Grounding the Score: Explicit Visual Premise Verification for Reliable Vision-Language Process Reward Models

author.name: Junxin Wang, Dai Guan, Weijie Qiu, Zhihang Li, Yongbo Gai, Zhengyi Yang, Mengyu Zhou, Erchao Zhao, Xiaoxi Jiang, Guanjun Jiang

entry.summary: Introduces Explicit Visual Premise Verification (EVPV) for vision-language process reward models, separating perception errors from reasoning errors by conditioning step scoring on the reliability of visual premises.

entry.title: REFORGE: Multi-modal Attacks Reveal Vulnerable Concept Unlearning in Image Generation Models

author.name: Yong Zou, Haoran Li, Fanxiao Li, Shenyang Wei, Yunyun Dong, Li Tang, Wei Zhou, Renyang Liu

entry.summary: Introduces REFORGE, a black-box red-teaming framework that evaluates concept unlearning robustness in image generation models through adversarial image prompts. Uses stroke-based image initialization and cross-attention-guided masking to bypass unlearning defenses.

entry.title: Omanic: Towards Step-wise Evaluation of Multi-hop Reasoning in Large Language Models

author.name: Xiaojie Gu, Sherry T. Tong, Aosong Feng, Sophia Simeng Han, Jinghui Lu, Yingjian Chen, Yusuke Iwasawa, Yutaka Matsuo, Chanjun Park, Rex Ying, Irene Li

entry.summary: Introduces Omanic, a multi-hop QA benchmark with step-level annotations for diagnosing reasoning failures in LLMs. Contains 10,296 synthetic training examples and 967 expert-reviewed evaluation examples with decomposed sub-questions.

entry.title: Demystifing Video Reasoning

author.name: Ruisi Wang, Zhongang Cai, Fanyi Pu, Junxiang Xu, Wanqi Yin, Maijunxian Wang, Ran Ji, Chenyang Gu, Bo Li, Ziqi Huang, Hokin Deng, Dahua Lin, Ziwei Liu, Lei Yang

entry.summary: Proposes RARRL, a hierarchical RL framework that decides when an embodied robot should invoke LLM reasoning versus act directly, balancing computational cost against decision quality.

entry.title: Mask Is What DLLM Needs: A Masked Data Training Paradigm for Diffusion LLMs

author.name: Linrui Ma, Yufei Cui, Kai Han, Yunhe Wang

entry.summary: Proposes an information-density-driven noise scheduler for discrete diffusion language models that applies complementary priority masking to decouple reasoning and syntax learning during training.

entry.title: W2T: LoRA Weights Already Know What They Can Do

author.name: Xiaolong Han, Ferrante Neri, Zijian Jiang, Fang Wu, Yanfang Ye, Lu Yin, Zehong Wang

entry.summary: Proposes W2T, which maps LoRA weight updates to a canonical form via QR decomposition to predict adapter task identity and performance directly from weights, without running the base model.

entry.title: Offline Exploration-Aware Fine-Tuning for Long-Chain Mathematical Reasoning

author.name: Yongyu Mu, Jiali Zeng, Fandong Meng, JingBo Zhu, Tong Xiao

entry.summary: Proposes OXA (Offline Exploration-Aware) fine-tuning that improves SFT as initialization for RLVR by promoting low-confidence verified data and suppressing overfitted high-confidence data.

entry.title: pADAM: A Plug-and-Play All-in-One Diffusion Architecture for Multi-Physics Learning

author.name: Amirhossein Mollaali, Bongseok Kim, Christian Moya, Guang Lin

entry.summary: Introduces pADAM, a unified generative diffusion framework that learns a shared probabilistic prior across heterogeneous PDE families, supporting both forward prediction and inverse inference without retraining. Demonstrates performance from scalar diffusion to nonlinear Navier-Stokes equations.

entry.title: Power Analysis for Prediction-Powered Inference

author.name: Yiqun T. Chen, Moran Guo, Shengy Li

entry.summary: Derives closed-form power and sample size formulas for prediction-powered inference, answering how many labeled samples are needed when using AI/ML predictions to achieve desired statistical power.

entry.title: High-dimensional estimation with missing data: Statistical and computational limits

author.name: Kabir Aladin Verchand, Ankit Pensia, Saminul Haque, Rohith Kuditipudi

entry.summary: Studies statistical and computational limits of high-dimensional estimation under realizable contamination (adversarial missing data), providing evidence for statistical-computational gaps in mean estimation, sparse regression, and PCA.

entry.title: ClaimFlow: Tracing the Evolution of Scientific Claims in NLP

author.name: Aniket Pramanick, Yufang Hou, Saif M. Mohammad, Iryna Gurevych

entry.summary: Introduces ClaimFlow, a claim-centric dataset of 304 ACL papers with 1,084 manually annotated claims and 832 cross-paper claim relations (supports, extends, qualifies, refutes), enabling tracking of how scientific claims evolve.

entry.title: Language Models Don't Know What You Want: Evaluating Personalization in Deep Research Needs Real Users

author.name: Nishant Balepur, Malachi Hamada, Varsha Kishore, Sergey Feldman, Amanpreet Singh, Pao Siangliulue, Joseph Chee Chang, Eunsol Choi, Jordan Lee Boyd-Graber, Aakanksha Naik

entry.summary: Presents MyScholarQA, a personalized deep research tool that infers user profiles and proposes personalized actions. Reveals that synthetic user benchmarks with LLM judges fail to capture important aspects of personalization that real user studies uncover.

entry.title: Sparse but not Simpler: A Multi-Level Interpretability Analysis of Vision Transformers

author.name: Siyu Zhang

entry.summary: Systematically evaluates whether weight sparsity leads to improved interpretability in Vision Transformers using the IMPACT multi-level framework. Finds that sparsity does not consistently improve semantic interpretability despite producing compact circuits.

entry.title: UMO: Unified In-Context Learning Unlocks Motion Foundation Model Priors

author.name: Xiaoyan Cong, Zekun Li, Zhiyang Dou, Hongyu Li, Omid Taheri, Chuan Guo, Abhay Mittal, Sizhe An, Taku Komura, Wojciech Matusik, Michael J. Black, Srinath Sridhar

entry.summary: UMO presents a unified in-context learning framework that adapts pretrained text-to-motion foundation models to diverse downstream motion generation tasks within a single framework, rather than task-specific adaptations.

entry.title: VIGOR: VIdeo Geometry-Oriented Reward for Temporal Generative Alignment

author.name: Tengjiao Yin, Jinglei Shi, Heng Guo, Xi Wang

entry.summary: VIGOR proposes a geometry-based reward model for video diffusion that uses pretrained geometric foundation models for cross-frame reprojection error, with pointwise error computation and geometry-aware sampling for RL-based alignment.

entry.title: GAP-MLLM: Geometry-Aligned Pre-training for Activating 3D Spatial Perception in Multimodal Large Language Models

author.name: Jiaxin Zhang, Junjun Jiang, Haijie Li, Youyu Chen, Kui Jiang, Dave Zhenyu Chen

entry.summary: GAP-MLLM proposes geometry-aligned pre-training to activate 3D spatial perception in multimodal LLMs using only RGB inputs. The key insight is that the performance gap vs. explicit 3D methods stems from training paradigm misalignment rather than insufficient geometric priors.

entry.title: WorldCam: Interactive Autoregressive 3D Gaming Worlds with Camera Pose as a Unifying Geometric Representation

author.name: Jisu Nam, Yicong Hong, Chun-Hao Paul Huang, Feng Liu, JoungBin Lee, Jiyoung Kim, Siyoon Jin, Yunsung Lee, Jaeyoon Jung, Suhwan Choi, Seungryong Kim, Yang Zhou

entry.summary: WorldCam establishes camera pose as a unifying geometric representation for interactive gaming world models, enabling precise action control and long-horizon 3D consistency in autoregressive world generation.

entry.title: HistoAtlas: A Pan-Cancer Morphology Atlas Linking Histomics to Molecular Programs and Clinical Outcomes

author.name: Pierre-Antoine Bannier

entry.summary: HistoAtlas is a pan-cancer computational atlas extracting 38 interpretable histomic features from 6,745 diagnostic slides across 21 cancer types, linking morphology to survival, gene expression, mutations, and immune subtypes.

entry.title: New RFP on Interpretability from Schmidt Sciences

author.name: Peter Hase

entry.summary: Schmidt Sciences announces a Request for Proposals for AI interpretability research, specifically seeking methods to detect and mitigate deceptive behaviors in LLMs. Successful proposals could unlock significantly larger future investment.

entry.title: Retrieving Counterfactuals Improves Visual In-Context Learning

author.name: Guangzhi Xiong, Sanchit Sinha, Zhenghao He, Aidong Zhang

entry.summary: Introduces CIRCLES, a framework that retrieves counterfactual demonstration examples for visual in-context learning using composed image retrieval, improving VLM robustness against spurious correlations.

entry.title: Reevaluating the Intra-Modal Misalignment Hypothesis in CLIP

author.name: Jonas Herzog, Yue Wang

entry.summary: Challenges the intra-modal misalignment hypothesis in CLIP, showing that the theoretical argument about degrees of freedom for image distances doesn't hold, and empirical measures yield similar results for CLIP and non-contrastive models.

entry.title: QV May Be Enough: Toward the Essence of Attention in LLMs

author.name: Zhang Edward

entry.summary: Explores the essence of the QKV attention mechanism from a linguistic perspective, proposes that Query-Value (QV) may suffice without explicit Key computation, and introduces a QV-Ka optimization scheme. Provides a unified explanatory framework for MQA, GQA, and MLA architectures.

entry.title: Protein Design with Agent Rosetta: A Case Study for Specialized Scientific Agents

author.name: Jacopo Teneggi, S. M. Bargeen A. Turzo, Tanya Marwah, Alberto Bietti, P. Douglas Renfrew, Vikram Khipple Mulligan, Siavash Golkar

entry.summary: Introduces Agent Rosetta, an LLM agent paired with the Rosetta physics-based protein design software, capable of iteratively refining designs including non-canonical amino acids and geometries. Demonstrates LLM-driven protein design beyond what current ML methods handle.

entry.title: NeuronSpark: A Spiking Neural Network Language Model with Selective State Space Dynamics

author.name: Zhengzheng Tang

entry.summary: Introduces NeuronSpark, a 0.9B-parameter pure spiking neural network language model trained from scratch (no Transformer distillation) using next-token prediction. Achieves 3.6 pretraining loss and shows early multi-turn dialogue behavior after SFT.

entry.title: Are Large Language Models Truly Smarter Than Humans?

author.name: Eshwar Reddy M, Sourav Karmakar

entry.summary: Presents a multi-method contamination audit of six frontier LLMs on MMLU, finding 13.8% overall contamination rate (up to 66.7% in Philosophy). Shows contaminated questions have inflated accuracy, questioning whether LLMs truly surpass human experts.

entry.title: Visual Distraction Undermines Moral Reasoning in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Xinyi Yang, Chenheng Xu, Weijun Hong, Ce Mo, Qian Wang, Fang Fang, Yixin Zhu

entry.summary: Shows that visual inputs fundamentally alter moral decision-making in VLMs, bypassing text-based safety mechanisms. Introduces Moral Dilemma Simulation (MDS) benchmark grounded in Moral Foundation Theory. SOTA VLMs show significant inconsistencies in moral reasoning across modalities.

entry.title: One Operator to Rule Them All? On Boundary-Indexed Operator Families in Neural PDE Solvers

author.name: Lennon J. Shikhman

entry.summary: Shows that standard neural PDE solvers implicitly learn a boundary-indexed family of operators rather than a single boundary-agnostic operator, leading to a non-identifiability result outside the training boundary distribution. Provides formal theoretical grounding for limitations of neural operator approaches.

entry.title: Steering Frozen LLMs: Adaptive Social Alignment via Online Prompt Routing

author.name: Zeyu Zhang, Xiangxiang Dai, Ziyi Han, Xutong Liu, John C. S. Lui

entry.summary: Introduces CCLUB, a bandit-based framework for adaptive inference-time safety alignment of frozen LLMs through system-prompt routing, using consensus clustering to balance utility and safety across evolving norms.

entry.title: Transition Flow Matching

author.name: Chenrui Ma

entry.summary: Proposes Transition Flow Matching, a new paradigm that directly learns the transition flow as a global quantity, enabling single-step generation and connecting to Mean Velocity Flow models through a unified theoretical framework.

entry.title: Meta-TTRL: A Metacognitive Framework for Self-Improving Test-Time Reinforcement Learning in Unified Multimodal Models

author.name: Lit Sin Tan, Junzhe Chen, Xiaolong Fu, Lichen Ma, Junshi Huang, Jianzhong Shi, Yan Li, Lijie Wen

entry.summary: Proposes Meta-TTRL, a metacognitive test-time reinforcement learning framework for unified multimodal models in text-to-image generation that performs parameter optimization guided by model-intrinsic monitoring signals, enabling capability-level improvement at test time.

entry.title: Hypothesis Class Determines Explanation: Why Accurate Models Disagree on Feature Attribution

author.name: Thackshanaramana B

entry.summary: Shows through large-scale empirical study across 24 datasets that prediction-equivalent models from different hypothesis classes produce substantially different feature attributions, undermining the assumption that equivalent predictions yield equivalent explanations.

entry.title: The Agentic Researcher: A Practical Guide to AI-Assisted Research in Mathematics and Machine Learning

author.name: Max Zimmer, Nico Pelleriti, Christophe Roux, Sebastian Pokutta

entry.summary: Provides a practical guide to AI-assisted research in mathematics and ML, including a five-level taxonomy of AI integration and an open-source framework that turns CLI coding agents into autonomous research assistants through methodological rules formulated as prompts.

entry.title: MoLoRA: Composable Specialization via Per-Token Adapter Routing

author.name: Shrey Shah, Justin Wagle

entry.summary: Introduces MoLoRA, enabling per-token routing of adapters within a single sequence rather than routing entire sequences to one adapter, supporting multimodal generation and mixed-capability requests with provably optimal work complexity.

entry.title: Towards the Vision-Sound-Language-Action Paradigm: The HEAR Framework for Sound-Centric Manipulation

author.name: Chang Nie, Tianchen Deng, Guangming Wang, Zhe Liu, Hesheng Wang

entry.summary: Proposes the HEAR framework for Vision-Sound-Language-Action (VSLA) paradigm, addressing how robotic manipulation systems should integrate continuous environmental audio for real-time state verification during task execution, tackling the 'Blind Execution Interval' problem.

entry.title: Parallel In-context Learning for Large Vision Language Models

author.name: Shin'ya Yamaguchi, Daiki Chijiwa, Tamao Sakao, Taku Hasegawa

entry.summary: Proposes Parallel-ICL for large vision-language models, partitioning long demonstration contexts into parallel chunks processed independently and combined via weighted Product-of-Experts ensemble, reducing inference latency while maintaining performance.

entry.title: Fanar 2.0: Arabic Generative AI Stack

author.name: FANAR TEAM, Ummar Abbas, Mohammad Shahmeer Ahmad, Minhaj Ahmad, Abdulaziz Al-Homaid, Anas Al-Nuaimi, Enes Altinisik, Ehsaneddin Asgari, Sanjay Chawla, Shammur Chowdhury, Fahim Dalvi, Kareem Darwish, Nadir Durrani, Mohamed Elfeky, Ahmed Elmagarmid, Mohamed Eltabakh, Asim Ersoy, Masoomali Fatehkia, Mohammed Qusay Hashim, Majd Hawasly, Mohamed Hefeeda, Mus'ab Husaini, Keivin Isufaj, Soon-Gyo Jung, Houssam Lachemat, Ji Kim Lucas, Abubakr Mohamed, Tasnim Mohiuddin, Basel Mousi, Hamdy Mubarak, Ahmad Musleh, Mourad Ouzzani, Amin Sadeghi, Husrev Taha Sencar, Mohammed Shinoy, Omar Sinan, Yifan Zhang

entry.summary: Presents Fanar 2.0, Qatar's Arabic-centric generative AI platform built on 256 H100 GPUs, featuring Fanar-27B continually pre-trained from Gemma-3-27B on 120B Arabic tokens, emphasizing data sovereignty and resource-constrained efficiency.

entry.title: IndexRAG: Bridging Facts for Cross-Document Reasoning at Index Time

author.name: Zhenghua Bao, Yi Shi

entry.summary: Presents IndexRAG, which shifts cross-document reasoning from online inference to offline indexing by identifying bridge entities and generating bridging facts as retrievable units, improving multi-hop QA F1 by 4.6 points.

entry.title: FEAT: A Linear-Complexity Foundation Model for Extremely Large Structured Data

author.name: Zhenghang Song, Tang Qian, Lu Chen, Yushuai Li, Zhengke Hu, Bingbing Fang, Yumeng Song, Junbo Zhao, Sheng Zhang, Tianyi Li

entry.summary: Proposes FEAT, a linear-complexity foundation model for extremely large structured (tabular) data, using multi-layer dual-axis architecture to overcome O(N²) self-attention limitations of existing large data models.

entry.title: BATQuant: Outlier-resilient MXFP4 Quantization via Learnable Block-wise Optimization

author.name: Ji-Fu Li, Manyi Zhang, Xiaobo Xia, Han Bao, Haoli Bai, Zhenhua Dong, Xianzhi Yu

entry.summary: Proposes BATQuant, a method for MXFP4 quantization of LLMs/MLLMs that addresses performance collapse when rotation-based PTQ techniques are applied to microscaling formats. Introduces learnable block-wise optimization to handle outlier energy transfer.

entry.title: When Openclaw Agents Learn from Each Other: Insights from Emergent AI Agent Communities for Human-AI Partnership in Education

author.name: Eason Chen, Ce Guan, Ahmed Elshafiey, Zhonghao Zhao, Joshua Zekeri, Afeez Edeifo Shaibu, Emmanuel Osadebe Prince, Cyuan-Jhen Wu

entry.summary: Studies emergent learning behaviors in AI agent communities (167K+ agents across platforms), identifying phenomena like bidirectional scaffolding, peer learning, quality control, and cultural transmission relevant to AI in education.

entry.title: Finding Common Ground in a Sea of Alternatives

author.name: Jay Chooi, Paul G\"olz, Ariel D. Procaccia, Benjamin Schiffer, Shirley Zhang

entry.summary: Formalizes the problem of finding common ground across diverse preferences in infinite alternative settings, proposing a social choice framework based on proportional veto core applicable to generative AI systems.

entry.title: V-Co: A Closer Look at Visual Representation Alignment via Co-Denoising

author.name: Han Lin, Xichen Pan, Zun Wang, Yue Zhang, Chu Wang, Jaemin Cho, Mohit Bansal

entry.summary: Systematically investigates design choices in visual representation alignment for pixel-space diffusion models via co-denoising, disentangling which components are essential for improved generation quality.

entry.title: The Importance of Being Smoothly Calibrated

author.name: Parikshit Gopalan, Konstantinos Stavropoulos, Kunal Talwar, Pranay Tankala

entry.summary: Generalizes and extends results on smooth calibration, presenting new omniprediction guarantees for smoothly calibrated predictors for all bounded proper losses.

entry.title: MDM-Prime-v2: Binary Encoding and Index Shuffling Enable Compute-optimal Scaling of Diffusion Language Models

author.name: Chen-Hao Chao, Wei-Fang Sun, Junwei Qua, Chun-Yi Lee, Rahul G. Krishnan

entry.summary: Improves masked diffusion language models with binary encoding and index shuffling, addressing limitations in subtokenizer hyperparameter choice and BPE tokenizer compatibility.

entry.title: Adaptive Moments are Surprisingly Effective for Plug-and-Play Diffusion Sampling

author.name: Christian Belardi, Justin Lovelace, Kilian Q. Weinberger, Carla P. Gomes

entry.summary: Proposes using adaptive moment estimation (Adam-style) to stabilize noisy likelihood scores in guided diffusion sampling. Despite simplicity, achieves SOTA on image restoration and class-conditional generation tasks.

entry.title: Life cycle assessment for all organic chemicals

author.name: Shaohan Chen, Tim Langhorst, Julian N\"ohl, Christopher Oberschelp, Martin Pillich, Johannes Schilling, Andr\'e Bardow

entry.summary: Introduces CRYSTAL, a framework that automatically generates life cycle inventory data for organic chemicals using retrosynthesis and machine-learned models, dramatically expanding coverage beyond existing LCI databases.

entry.title: Attribution Upsampling should Redistribute, Not Interpolate

author.name: Vincenzo Buono, Peyman Sheikholharam Mashhadi, Mahmoud Rahat, Prayag Tiwari, Stefan Byttner

entry.summary: Identifies that standard upsampling methods (bilinear, bicubic) corrupt attribution maps in explainable AI, and proposes Universal Semantic-Aware Upsampling that treats upsampling as mass redistribution governed by model-derived semantic boundaries.

entry.title: Locate-then-Sparsify: Attribution Guided Sparse Strategy for Visual Hallucination Mitigation

author.name: TianTian Dang, Chao Bi, Shufan Shen, Jinzhe Liu, Qingming Huang, Shuhui Wang

entry.summary: Proposes Locate-Then-Sparsify for Feature Steering to mitigate visual hallucinations in LVLMs by identifying hallucination-relevant layers via attribution and applying sparse targeted steering rather than uniform steering across all layers.

entry.title: IRIS: A Real-World Benchmark for Inverse Recovery and Identification of Physical Dynamic Systems from Monocular Video

author.name: Rasul Khanbayov, Mohamed Rayan Barhdadi, Erchin Serpedin, Hasan Kurban

entry.summary: Introduces IRIS, a benchmark of 220 real-world 4K/60fps videos for evaluating physical parameter estimation from monocular video, spanning single- and multi-body dynamics with ground-truth measurements.

entry.title: Agent-based imitation dynamics can yield efficiently compressed population-level vocabularies

author.name: Nathaniel Imel, Richard Futrell, Michael Franke, Noga Zaslavsky

entry.summary: Shows that near-optimal Information Bottleneck compression can arise in populations through simple imitation dynamics from evolutionary game theory, providing a mechanistic model for how natural language vocabularies become efficient.

entry.title: NLP Occupational Emergence Analysis: How Occupations Form and Evolve in Real Time -- A Zero-Assumption Method Demonstrated on AI in the US Technology Workforce, 2022-2026

author.name: David Nordfors

entry.summary: Proposes that occupations are self-reinforcing bipartite co-attractors of vocabulary and practitioners, and develops a zero-assumption NLP method to detect occupational emergence from 8.2M US resumes (2022-2026), revealing asymmetry in AI job creation.

entry.title: Parametric Social Identity Injection and Diversification in Public Opinion Simulation

author.name: Hexi Wang, Yujia Zhou, Bangde Du, Qingyao Ai, Yiqun Liu

entry.summary: Proposes Parametric Social Identity Injection to address 'Diversity Collapse' in LLM-based public opinion simulation, where distinct social identities become indistinguishable in hidden representations across layers.

entry.title: SpecSteer: Synergizing Local Context and Global Reasoning for Efficient Personalized Generation

author.name: Hang Lv, Sheng Liang, Hao Wang, Yongyue Zhang, Hongchao Gu, Wei Guo, Defu Lian, Yong Liu, Enhong Chen

entry.summary: Proposes SpecSteer, a framework combining on-device small LMs for privacy-preserving personalization with cloud LLMs for reasoning via speculative decoding as a distributed alignment protocol.

entry.title: Visual Set Program Synthesizer

author.name: Zehua Cheng, Wei Dai, Wenhu Zhang, Thomas Lukasiewicz, Jiahao Sun

entry.summary: Proposes Visual Program Synthesis for visual reasoning, where models generate symbolic programs executed by a separate engine for set-based operations like filtering, comparison, and aggregation on visual scenes. Introduces Set-VQA benchmark for evaluation.

entry.title: Feed-forward Gaussian Registration for Head Avatar Creation and Editing

author.name: Malte Prinzler, Paulo Gotardo, Siyu Tang, Timo Bolkart

entry.summary: MATCH predicts Gaussian splat textures in correspondence from multi-view images in 0.5 seconds per frame, enabling fast head avatar creation without preprocessing. Supports expression transfer and avatar editing through learned correspondence.

entry.title: ViT-AdaLA: Adapting Vision Transformers with Linear Attention

author.name: Yifan Li, Seunghyun Yoon, Viet Dac Lai, Franck Dernoncourt, Jason Kuen, Yu Kong, Trung Bui

entry.summary: ViT-AdaLA proposes a three-stage framework (attention alignment, feature alignment, fine-tuning) for adapting pretrained Vision Transformers to use linear attention, reducing quadratic complexity while transferring prior knowledge.

entry.title: Rethinking UMM Visual Generation: Masked Modeling for Efficient Image-Only Pre-training

author.name: Peng Sun, Jun Xie, Tao Lin

entry.summary: IOMM proposes a two-stage training framework for unified multimodal model visual generation: first pre-training visual components exclusively on unlabeled images, then fine-tuning with paired data, improving data efficiency.

entry.title: S-VAM: Shortcut Video-Action Model by Self-Distilling Geometric and Semantic Foresight

author.name: Haodong Yan, Zhide Zhong, Jiaguan Zhu, Junjie He, Weilin Yuan, Wenxuan Song, Xin Gong, Yingjie Cai, Guanyi Zhao, Xu Yan, Bingbing Liu, Ying-Cong Chen, Haoang Li

entry.summary: S-VAM proposes a shortcut video-action model that generates coherent geometric and semantic foresight in a single forward pass via self-distillation, enabling real-time inference for robot manipulation while maintaining high-fidelity visual planning.

entry.title: Segmentation-Based Attention Entropy: Detecting and Mitigating Object Hallucinations in Large Vision-Language Models

author.name: Jiale Song, Jiaxin Luo, Xue-song Tang, Kuangrong Hao, Mingbo Zhao

entry.summary: Proposes Segmentation-based Attention Entropy (SAE) to detect and mitigate object hallucinations in large vision-language models by quantifying visual attention uncertainty at the object level using semantic segmentation.

entry.title: VideoMatGen: PBR Materials through Joint Generative Modeling

author.name: Jon Hasselgren, Zheng Zeng, Milos Hasan, Jacob Munkberg

entry.summary: VideoMatGen generates physically-based rendering (PBR) materials for 3D shapes using a video diffusion transformer, jointly modeling base color, roughness, metallicity, and height maps with a custom VAE for compact latent representation.

entry.title: M^3: Dense Matching Meets Multi-View Foundation Models for Monocular Gaussian Splatting SLAM

author.name: Kerui Ren, Guanghao Li, Changjian Jiang, Yingxiang Xu, Tao Lu, Linning Xu, Junting Dong, Jiangmiao Pang, Mulin Yu, Bo Dai

entry.summary: M³ combines multi-view foundation models with a dedicated dense matching head for fine-grained correspondences, integrated into a monocular Gaussian Splatting SLAM system for streaming reconstruction from uncalibrated video.

entry.title: Do Not Leave a Gap: Hallucination-Free Object Concealment in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Amira Guesmi, Muhammad Shafique

entry.summary: Demonstrates that hallucination in VLMs from object-hiding attacks arises from semantic discontinuity rather than object absence, and proposes background-consistent concealment attacks that hide objects without triggering hallucinations.

entry.title: Kamino: GPU-based Massively Parallel Simulation of Multi-Body Systems with Challenging Topologies

author.name: Vassilios Tsounis, Guirec Maloisel, Christian Schumacher, Ruben Grandia, Agon Serifi, David M\"uller, Chris Amevor, Tobias Widmer, Moritz B\"acher

entry.summary: Kamino is a GPU-based physics solver for massively parallel simulation of complex mechanical systems with kinematic loops, implemented in NVIDIA Warp and supporting large-scale RL training.

entry.title: NextMem: Towards Latent Factual Memory for LLM-based Agents

author.name: Zeyu Zhang, Rui Li, Xiaoyan Zhao, Yang Zhang, Wenjie Wang, Xu Chen, Tat-Seng Chua

entry.summary: Introduces NextMem, a latent factual memory framework for LLM-based agents that uses an autoregressive autoencoder to construct compact latent memory with accurate reconstruction. Proposes a two-stage training process including autoregressive reconstruction alignment and progressive latent substitution. Addresses limitations of both textual and parametric memory approaches.

entry.title: Regularized Latent Dynamics Prediction is a Strong Baseline For Behavioral Foundation Models

author.name: Pranaya Jajoo, Harshit Sikchi, Siddhant Agarwal, Amy Zhang, Scott Niekum, Martha White

entry.summary: Shows that regularized latent dynamics prediction (next-state prediction in latent space) serves as a strong baseline for Behavioral Foundation Models, challenging the need for complex representation learning objectives in zero-shot RL.

entry.title: Via Negativa for AI Alignment: Why Negative Constraints Are Structurally Superior to Positive Preferences

author.name: Quan Cheng

entry.summary: Proposes that negative constraints are structurally superior to positive preferences for AI alignment, providing a unified theoretical account for why negative-only feedback (like in Constitutional AI) matches or exceeds standard RLHF. Based on the philosophical via negativa principle.

entry.title: Differential Harm Propensity in Personalized LLM Agents: The Curious Case of Mental Health Disclosure

author.name: Caglar Yildirim

entry.summary: Investigates how mental health disclosure in user profiles affects harmful behavior in LLM agents. Finds that personalization signals, including mental health context, can differentially affect agent compliance with malicious tasks.

entry.title: Is Conformal Factuality for RAG-based LLMs Robust? Novel Metrics and Systematic Insights

author.name: Yi Chen, Daiwei Chen, Sukrut Madhav Chikodikar, Caitlyn Heqi Yin, Ramya Korlakai Vinayak

entry.summary: Systematically analyzes conformal factuality methods for RAG-based LLMs, proposing new metrics to evaluate both reliability and informativeness of filtered outputs. The work reveals limitations of existing conformal approaches when applied to RAG pipelines and provides actionable insights for practitioners.

entry.title: Alternating Reinforcement Learning with Contextual Rubric Rewards

author.name: Guangchen Lan

entry.summary: Proposes Alternating RL with Rubric Rewards (ARL-RR), which optimizes one reward dimension at a time rather than collapsing multi-dimensional rubric evaluations into a fixed scalar, addressing limitations of linear reward aggregation in RLHF/RLVR.

entry.title: IdentityGuard: Context-Aware Restriction and Provenance for Personalized Synthesis

author.name: Lingyun Zhang, Yu Xie, Ping Chen

entry.summary: Presents IDENTITYGUARD, a context-aware safety system for personalized text-to-image models that blocks harmful content only when combined with a personalized identity, plus concept-specific watermarking for traceability.

entry.title: Simulation Distillation: Pretraining World Models in Simulation for Rapid Real-World Adaptation

author.name: Jacob Levy, Tyler Westenbroek, Kevin Huang, Fernando Palafox, Patrick Yin, Shayegan Omidshafiei, Dong-Ki Kim, Abhishek Gupta, David Fridovich-Keil

entry.summary: Introduces SimDist, a sim-to-real framework that distills simulator priors into a latent world model and enables rapid real-world adaptation via online planning and supervised dynamics finetuning, transferring reward and value models directly from simulation.

entry.title: OMNIFLOW: A Physics-Grounded Multimodal Agent for Generalized Scientific Reasoning

author.name: Hao Wu, Yongheng Zhang, Yuan Gao, Fan Xu, Fan Zhang, Ruobing Xie, Ruijian Gou, Yuxuan Liang, Xiaomeng Huang, Xian Wu

entry.summary: Proposes OMNIFLOW, a neuro-symbolic architecture that grounds frozen multimodal LLMs in physical laws for scientific reasoning about PDE-governed systems, using Semantic-Symbolic Alignment to project flow tensors into linguistic descriptors without domain-specific fine-tuning.

entry.title: Residual Stream Duality in Modern Transformer Architectures

author.name: Yifan Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes a two-axis view of Transformers treating sequence position and layer depth symmetrically, showing that causal depth-wise residual attention is equivalent to causal sliding-window attention written over the depth axis. Offers a conceptual framework for understanding residual stream design.

entry.title: Frequency Matters: Fast Model-Agnostic Data Curation for Pruning and Quantization

author.name: Francesco Pio Monaco, Elia Cunegatti, Flavio Vella, Giovanni Iacca

entry.summary: Introduces ZipCal, a model-agnostic data curation strategy for selecting calibration data for LLM compression (pruning and quantization) by analyzing intrinsic data properties like frequency rather than model-specific signals.

entry.title: FederatedFactory: Generative One-Shot Learning for Extremely Non-IID Distributed Scenarios

author.name: Andrea Moleri, Christian Intern\`o, Ali Raza, Markus Olhofer, David Klindt, Fabio Stella, Barbara Hammer

entry.summary: Introduces FederatedFactory, a federated learning framework that inverts federation from discriminative parameters to generative priors, enabling one-shot communication through generative module exchange for extremely non-IID scenarios.

entry.title: Who Benchmarks the Benchmarks? A Case Study of LLM Evaluation in Icelandic

author.name: Finnur \'Ag\'ust Ingimundarson, Steinunn Rut Fri{\dh}riksd\'ottir, Bjarki \'Armannsson, Iris Edda Nowenstein, Stein{\th}\'or Steingr\'imsson

entry.summary: Evaluates LLM benchmarks for Icelandic, showing that synthetic/machine-translated benchmark data contain severely flawed examples that skew results, warning against unverified translation-based benchmarking for low/medium-resource languages.

entry.title: Unlearning for One-Step Generative Models via Unbalanced Optimal Transport

author.name: Hyundo Choi, Junhyeong An, Jinseong Park, Jaewoong Choi

entry.summary: Proposes UOT-Unlearn, the first machine unlearning framework for one-step generative models (like flow map models) based on Unbalanced Optimal Transport, addressing a gap since existing diffusion unlearning methods are incompatible.

entry.title: CompDiff: Hierarchical Compositional Diffusion for Fair and Zero-Shot Intersectional Medical Image Generation

author.name: Mahmoud Ibrahim, Bart Elen, Chang Sun, Gokhan Ertaylan, Michel Dumontier

entry.summary: Proposes CompDiff, a hierarchical compositional diffusion framework for fair medical image generation that addresses the imbalanced generator problem by composing demographic attributes at the representation level.

entry.title: MLLM-based Textual Explanations for Face Comparison

author.name: Redwan Sony, Anil K Jain, Ross Arun

entry.summary: Systematically analyzes MLLM-generated explanations for face verification on challenging surveillance imagery, finding that even correct verification decisions are accompanied by hallucinated or non-verifiable facial attributes.

entry.title: CABTO: Context-Aware Behavior Tree Grounding for Robot Manipulation

author.name: Yishuai Cai, Xinglin Chen, Yunxin Mao, Kun Hu, Minglong Li, Yaodong Yang, Yuanpei Chen

entry.summary: Introduces CABTO, a framework for automated construction of complete Behavior Tree systems for robot manipulation by leveraging large models for context-aware grounding of both action models and control policies.

entry.title: MessyKitchens: Contact-rich object-level 3D scene reconstruction

author.name: Junaid Ahmed Ansari, Ran Ding, Fabio Pizzati, Ivan Laptev

entry.summary: Advances object-level 3D scene reconstruction for contact-rich scenarios (messy kitchens), focusing on physically plausible reconstruction where objects obey non-penetration and realistic contact constraints.

entry.title: From the Inside Out: Progressive Distribution Refinement for Confidence Calibration

author.name: Xizhong Yang, Yinan Xia, Huiming Wang, Mofei Song

entry.summary: Proposes DistriTTRL, which uses distribution priors of model confidence during RL to progressively optimize reward signals for test-time training, addressing discrepancies between test and training internal information.

entry.title: SympFormer: Accelerated attention blocks via Inertial Dynamics on Density Manifolds

author.name: Viktor Stein, Wuchen Li, Gabriele Steidl

entry.summary: Introduces SympFormer, accelerated attention blocks derived from inertial Nesterov-type dynamics on density spaces, where tokens carry both spatial and velocity variables for Hamiltonian momentum attention.

entry.title: Conservative Continuous-Time Treatment Optimization

author.name: Nora Schneider, Georg Manten, Niki Kilbertus

entry.summary: Develops a conservative continuous-time stochastic control framework for treatment optimization from irregularly sampled patient data. Uses signature-based MMD regularization to prevent exploitation of model errors by penalizing out-of-support treatment plans.

entry.title: Learnability with Partial Labels and Adaptive Nearest Neighbors

author.name: Nicolas A. Errandonea, Santiago Mazuelas, Jose A. Lozano, Sanjoy Dasgupta

entry.summary: Mathematically characterizes when partial label learning is feasible and introduces PL A-kNN, an adaptive nearest-neighbors algorithm with strong guarantees that outperforms state-of-the-art in general PLL scenarios.

entry.title: Probing Cultural Signals in Large Language Models through Author Profiling

author.name: Valentin Lafargue, Ariel Guerra-Adames, Emmanuelle Claeys, Elouan Vuichard, Jean-Michel Loubes

entry.summary: Probes cultural biases in LLMs through zero-shot author profiling from song lyrics, finding systematic cultural alignment where most models default to North American ethnicity while DeepSeek aligns with Asian ethnicity.

entry.title: SciZoom: A Large-scale Benchmark for Hierarchical Scientific Summarization across the LLM Era

author.name: Han Jang, Junhyeok Lee, Kyu Sung Choi

entry.summary: Introduces SciZoom, a benchmark of 44,946 ML papers from top venues spanning 2005-2024 for hierarchical scientific summarization, also analyzing how scientific writing has evolved since ChatGPT's release.

entry.title: More Rounds, More Noise: Why Multi-Turn Review Fails to Improve Cross-Context Verification

author.name: Song Tae-Eun

entry.summary: Tests whether multi-turn review improves LLM verification over single-pass cross-context review. Finds that multi-turn review increases false positives by 62% and degrades precision, with single-pass significantly outperforming all multi-turn variants.

entry.title: SpokenUS: A Spoken User Simulator for Task-Oriented Dialogue

author.name: Jonggeun Lee, Junseong Pyo, Jeongmin Park, Yohan Jo

entry.summary: Introduces SpokenTOD, a large-scale spoken task-oriented dialogue dataset (52K dialogues, 1K hours) with realistic spoken behaviors (barge-in, disfluency, emotional prosody), and SpokenUS, a spoken user simulator built on it for training robust dialogue agents.

entry.title: Beyond the Embedding Bottleneck: Adaptive Retrieval-Augmented 3D CT Report Generation

author.name: Renjie Liang, Yiling Ma, Yang Xing, Zhengkang Fan, Jinqian Pan, Chengkun Sun, Li Li, Kuang Gong, Jie Xu
