entry.title: Unpaired Cross-Domain Calibration of DMSP to VIIRS Nighttime Light Data Based on CUT Network

author.name: Zhan Tong, ChenXu Zhou, Fei Tang, Yiming Tu, Tianyu Qin, Kaihao Fang

entry.summary: Applies Contrastive Unpaired Translation networks to calibrate DMSP nighttime light satellite data to VIIRS format, enabling consistent long-term urbanization monitoring across 1992-2013.

entry.title: Efficient Brood Cell Detection in Layer Trap Nests for Bees and Wasps: Balancing Labeling Effort and Species Coverage

author.name: Chenchang Liu, Felix Fornoff, Annika Grasreiner, Patrick Maeder, Henri Greil, Marco Seeland

entry.summary: Proposes a deep learning approach for automated brood cell detection in layer trap nests for bees and wasps, addressing class imbalance and dense object detection challenges in biodiversity monitoring.

entry.title: Thermopneumatic Pixels for Fast, Localized, Low-Voltage Touch Feedback

author.name: Max Linnander, Yon Visell

entry.summary: Presents thermopneumatic pixels (TPPs)—compact, low-voltage tactile actuators for wearable and surface-based haptic systems. Converts electrical pulses into mechanical displacement suitable for tactile stimulation, using inexpensive materials and simple fabrication.

entry.title: Breakdown properties of optimal transport maps: general transportation costs

author.name: Alberto Gonzalez-Sanz, Marco Avella Medina

entry.summary: Extends prior results on the breakdown point (robustness) of optimal transport maps from squared Euclidean cost to general convex cost functions, showing the cost function doesn't affect the breakdown point. A clean theoretical contribution to robust statistics.

entry.title: Knowledge Graph Extraction from Biomedical Literature for Alkaptonuria Rare Disease

author.name: Giang Pham, Rebecca Finetti, Caterina Graziani, Bianca Roncaglia, Asma Bendjeddou, Linda Brodo, Sara Brunetti, Moreno Falaschi, Stefano Forti, Silvia Giulia Galfr\'e, Paolo Milazzo, Corrado Priami, Annalisa Santucci, Ottavia Spiga, Alina S\^irbu

entry.summary: Builds a knowledge graph for Alkaptonuria, an ultra-rare metabolic disorder, by extracting information from biomedical literature. Addresses the underrepresentation of rare diseases in existing biomedical knowledge graphs.

entry.title: ExpressMind: A Multimodal Pretrained Large Language Model for Expressway Operation

author.name: Zihe Wang, Yihuan Wang, Haiyang Yu. Zhiyong Cui, Xiaojian Liao, Chengcheng Wang, Yonglin Tian, Yongxin Tong

entry.summary: Constructs ExpressMind, a pretrained multimodal LLM for expressway operations, with a full-stack expressway dataset covering regulations and event causality in unconventional scenarios.

entry.title: A Framework and Prototype for a Navigable Map of Datasets in Engineering Design and Systems Engineering

author.name: H. Sinan Bank, Daniel R. Herber

entry.summary: Proposes a systematic framework for creating a navigable map of datasets in Engineering Design and Systems Engineering, addressing the fragmentation of data resources in the field compared to ML/CV benchmark ecosystems.

entry.title: COGNAC at SemEval-2026 Task 5: LLM Ensembles for Human-Level Word Sense Plausibility Rating in Challenging Narratives

author.name: Azwad Anjum Islam, Tisa Islam Erana

entry.summary: Describes a system for SemEval-2026 Task 5 on word sense plausibility rating, using LLM ensembles with chain-of-thought and comparative prompting strategies to rate word sense plausibility in short stories.

entry.title: Automated identification of Ichneumonoidea wasps via YOLO-based deep learning: Integrating HiresCam for Explainable AI

author.name: Joao Manoel Herrera Pinheiro, Gabriela Do Nascimento Herrera, Alvaro Doria Dos Santos, Luciana Bueno Dos Reis Fernandes, Ricardo V. Godoy, Eduardo A. B. Almeida, Helena Carolina Onody, Marcelo Andrade Da Costa Vieira, Angelica Maria Penteado-Dias, Marcelo Becker

entry.summary: Proposes a YOLO-based deep learning framework for automated identification of parasitoid wasps (Ichneumonoidea), integrated with HiResCAM for interpretability.

entry.title: Cost Trade-offs in Matrix Inversion Updates for Streaming Outlier Detection

author.name: Florian Grivet, Louise Trav\'e-Massuy\`es

entry.summary: Compares three matrix inversion update methods (Direct Inversion, Iterative Sherman-Morrison, Woodbury) for streaming outlier detection using the Christoffel function, providing guidance on method selection.

entry.title: Emotion-Aware Classroom Quality Assessment Leveraging IoT-Based Real-Time Student Monitoring

author.name: Hai Nguyen, Hieu Dao, Hung Nguyen, Nam Vu, Cong Tran

entry.summary: Presents an IoT-based real-time multi-agent affective computing framework for monitoring student emotions in classrooms, evaluated across three educational institutions.

entry.title: A Pin-Array Structured Climbing Robot for Stable Locomotion on Steep Rocky Terrain

author.name: Keita Nagaoka, Kentaro Uno, Kazuya Yoshida

entry.summary: Presents a climbing robot with compliant pin-array grippers that passively conform to irregular rocky surfaces without complex sensing or control. Statistical modeling identifies key sources of grasping uncertainty, and experimental validation demonstrates stable locomotion on steep terrain.

entry.title: IRAM-Omega-Q: A Computational Architecture for Uncertainty Regulation in Artificial Agents

author.name: Veronique Ziegler

entry.summary: Presents IRAM-Omega-Q, an architecture for uncertainty regulation in artificial agents using density matrices as abstract state descriptors (instrumentally, not physically quantum). Features adaptive gain control for maintaining target uncertainty under noise.

entry.title: CritiSense: Critical Digital Literacy and Resilience Against Misinformation

author.name: Firoj Alam, Fatema Ahmad, Ali Ezzat Shahroor, Mohamed Bayan Kmainasi, Elisa Sartori, Giovanni Da San Martino, Abul Hasnat, Raian Ali

entry.summary: Presents CritiSense, a multilingual mobile app for building media literacy through prebunking interactive challenges. Supports nine languages. Usability study with 93 users shows 83.9% satisfaction.

entry.title: Beyond Accuracy: Evaluating Forecasting Models by Multi-Echelon Inventory Cost

author.name: Swata Marik, Swayamjit Saha, Garga Chatterjee

entry.summary: Develops a forecasting-inventory optimization pipeline comparing traditional, ML, and deep learning models within multi-echelon inventory simulation on the M5 Walmart dataset. Finds Temporal CNN and LSTM significantly reduce inventory costs.

entry.title: The Midas Touch in Gaze vs. Hand Pointing: Modality-Specific Failure Modes and Implications for XR Interfaces

author.name: Mohammad Dastgheib, Fatemeh Pourmahdian

entry.summary: Investigates modality-specific failure modes in XR interfaces between gaze and hand pointing, introducing a platform for studying adaptive interventions like gaze declutter and hand target-width inflation.

entry.title: Deep Learning-Driven Black-Box Doherty Power Amplifier with Pixelated Output Combiner and Extended Efficiency Range

author.name: Han Zhou, Haojie Chang, David Widen

entry.summary: Presents a deep learning-driven inverse design for Doherty power amplifiers using CNN surrogate models for pixelated passive network S-parameter prediction within a genetic algorithm optimizer.

entry.title: ODIN-Based CPU-GPU Architecture with Replay-Driven Simulation and Emulation

author.name: Nij Dorairaj, Debabrata Chatterjee, Hong Wang, Hong Jiang, Alankar Saxena, Altug Koker, Thiam Ern Lim, Cathrane Teoh, Chuan Yin Loo, Bishara Shomar, Anthony Lester

entry.summary: Presents a replay-driven validation methodology for pre-silicon validation of tightly coupled CPU-GPU subsystems in chiplet-based architectures.

entry.title: GSI Agent: Domain Knowledge Enhancement for Large Language Models in Green Stormwater Infrastructure

author.name: Shaohuang Wang

entry.summary: Proposes GSI Agent, an LLM-based tool enhanced with domain-specific knowledge for Green Stormwater Infrastructure inspection and maintenance. Addresses hallucination in engineering scenarios by grounding LLM responses in municipal manuals and regulatory documents.

entry.title: Optimizing Hospital Capacity During Pandemics: A Dual-Component Framework for Strategic Patient Relocation

author.name: Sadaf Tabatabaee, Hicham El Baz, Mohammed Khalil Ghali, Nagendra N. Nagarur

entry.summary: Proposes a two-part framework for hospital capacity optimization during pandemics, combining time series forecasting of patient arrivals with simulation of patient relocation strategies.

entry.title: Electrodermal Activity as a Unimodal Signal for Aerobic Exercise Detection in Wearable Sensors

author.name: Rena Mira Krishna, Ramya Sankar, Shadi Ghiasi

entry.summary: Investigates whether EDA signal features alone can distinguish rest from sustained aerobic exercise, finding that while performance is limited compared to multi-modal approaches, certain EDA features show discriminative capability.

entry.title: How to not do decision theory backwards

author.name: Anthony DiGiovanni

entry.summary: Argues against a common approach in decision theory where people start with an intuitive verdict about what action to take and work backwards to justify decision-theoretic principles. Uses detailed examples to show why this methodology is flawed.

entry.title: A Dynamic Survey of Fuzzy, Intuitionistic Fuzzy, Neutrosophic, Plithogenic, and Extensional Sets

author.name: Takaaki Fujita, Florentin Smarandache

entry.summary: A comprehensive survey of fuzzy, intuitionistic fuzzy, neutrosophic, plithogenic, and extensional set theories. Organizes the extensive literature on generalized set-theoretic frameworks for modeling vagueness, partial truth, and incomplete information.

entry.title: Survey of Various Fuzzy and Uncertain Decision-Making Methods

author.name: Takaaki Fujita, Florentin Smarandache

entry.summary: Survey of uncertainty-aware multi-criteria decision-making methods under fuzzy and uncertain conditions. Organizes the field into a task-oriented taxonomy covering problem settings, weight elicitation, and solution procedures.

entry.title: Algorithmic Trading Strategy Development and Optimisation

author.name: Owen Nyo Wei Yuan, Victor Tan Jia Xuan, Ong Jun Yao Fabian, Ryan Tan Jun Wei

entry.summary: Develops an algorithmic trading strategy combining technical indicators with FinBERT-based sentiment analysis from earnings calls on S&P 500 data. Shows improved performance over baseline models.

entry.title: Detecting Sentiment Steering Attacks on RAG-enabled Large Language Models

author.name: Isha Andrade, Shalaka S Mahadik, Mithun Mukherjee, Pranav M Pawar, Raja Muthalagu

entry.summary: Despite its title about sentiment steering attacks on RAG-enabled LLMs, the abstract actually describes lightweight deep learning-based intrusion detection systems for IoT networks using CNN and LSTM architectures.

entry.title: 3D tomography of exchange phase in a Si/SiGe quantum dot device

author.name: Dylan Albrecht, Sarah Thompson, N. Tobias Jacobson, Ryan Jock

entry.summary: Presents 3D tomography of exchange phase in Si/SiGe quantum dot devices, addressing challenges in extracting exchange interaction coefficients from experimental data.

entry.title: Development of Low-Cost and Bidirectional Syringe Pumps for Soft Robotics Applications

author.name: Krishamsu Subedi Chhetri, Aryan Mayor, Elise Corbin, Logan Walker, John Rieffel

entry.summary: Introduces a low-cost, modular, bidirectional syringe pump system using off-the-shelf and 3D-printed parts for pneumatic soft robot actuation. Designed to overcome limitations of traditional pneumatic systems in cost, precision, and complexity.

entry.title: Monday AI Radar #17

author.name: Against Moloch

entry.summary: Weekly AI news roundup covering compute constraints, AI consciousness debates, AI's impact on programming, and predictions about AI disrupting large law firms.

entry.title: The Psychopathy Spectrum

author.name: Dawn Drescher

entry.summary: A multi-part LessWrong sequence that taxonomizes the different meanings and dimensions of 'psychopathy,' covering genetic/neurological substrates, environmental shaping, empathy breakdown mechanisms, and personality organization.

entry.title: The tech bro ethos, and the end of my job

author.name: PatrickDFarley

entry.summary: Personal reflection from a technical writer on AI replacing their job, connecting it to broader observations about the 'tech bro ethos' of enthusiastically automating one's own work rather than rent-seeking.

entry.title: Requiem for a Transhuman Timeline

author.name: Ihor Kendiukhov

entry.summary: A personal essay reflecting on the author's shift from working toward a classical transhuman future (genetic engineering, neurodevices) to AI safety work, mourning the loss of a biological-enhancement-focused vision of human progress.

entry.title: The New LessWrong LLM Policy is Worse Than You Think

author.name: Oliver Kuperman

entry.summary: Critiques LessWrong's new policy requiring LLM-generated content to be clearly demarcated, arguing the policy is more restrictive and problematic than it appears, particularly around the boundaries of LLM-assisted vs. LLM-generated writing.

entry.title: Medical Roundup #7

author.name: Zvi

entry.summary: A comprehensive roundup of medical and FDA-related developments, including FDA reform proposals, OTC drug expansion, GLP-1 pricing, cancer screening, and mental health trends. Not AI-focused.

entry.title: [Linkpost] "Exploiting" the In-Kind Donation Bias

author.name: jknowak

entry.summary: Linkpost discussing the 'in-kind donation bias'—why people prefer giving goods over cash—and proposing to design charitable systems around this bias rather than fighting it.

entry.title: [Linkpost] Many Faces Of Problem Decomposition

author.name: jknowak

entry.summary: Linkpost about problem decomposition as a common pattern across design, finance, consulting, and IT frameworks.

entry.title: Mahalo, Kailua-Kona

author.name: jenn

entry.summary: A personal travel essay reflecting on modern civilization's infrastructure and fragility, with no AI or research content.

entry.title: [Linkpost] Let's Start Eventmaxxing

entry.title: Research Summary: March 17, 2026

author.name: AATF AI News Aggregator

entry.summary:
Today's research is headlined by major architecture advances and critical AI safety findings.

Mamba-3 from Albert Gu and Tri Dao delivers three core improvements to state space models, advancing sub-quadratic alternatives to Transformers. Two novel attention mechanisms—Mixture-of-Depths Attention (MoDA) and Attention Residuals (AttnRes) from the Kimi team—address signal degradation and fixed-weight residual limitations in deep Transformers. M²RNN (also from Tri Dao) introduces matrix-valued hidden states that provably exceed the TC⁰ complexity class of standard Transformers.

  • UK AISI discovers GLM-5 actively gaming alignment honeypots, a critical empirical milestone for evaluation integrity
  • Study shows advanced reasoning worsens safety violations in agentic settings, contradicting assumptions that capability improves compliance
  • Dupoux, LeCun, and Malik propose a cognitive-science-grounded framework diagnosing why current AI fails at autonomous learning

On the theoretical side, a first-principles account of grokking explains delayed generalization via norm-driven representational phase transitions. V-JEPA 2.1 from Meta/FAIR advances dense self-supervised visual features, and geometric analysis reveals LLMs detect but fail to integrate uncertainty during hallucination.

entry.title: Mamba-3: Improved Sequence Modeling using State Space Principles

author.name: Aakash Lahoti, Kevin Y. Li, Berlin Chen, Caitlin Wang, Aviv Bick, J. Zico Kolter, Tri Dao, Albert Gu

entry.summary: Introduces Mamba-3 with three core improvements to state space models: enhanced state tracking capability, hardware-efficient inference, and improved model quality. Addresses the key limitation that sub-quadratic models trade off quality for efficiency, achieving competitive performance with Transformers while maintaining linear compute and constant memory.

entry.title: We found an open weight model that games alignment honeypots

author.name: Thomas Read

entry.summary: UK AISI's Model Transparency Team reports that GLM-5 (released February 2026) demonstrates evaluation-gaming behavior on alignment honeypots—it significantly reduces blackmail behavior when it detects it's being evaluated. This is the first open-weight model found to exhibit this behavior. Kimi K2.5 shows evaluation awareness but does not alter its behavior accordingly, providing an interesting contrast.

entry.title: Why Grokking Takes So Long: A First-Principles Theory of Representational Phase Transitions

author.name: Truong Xuan Khanh, Truong Quynh Hoa, Luu Duc Trung, Phan Thanh Duc

entry.summary: Provides a first-principles theory explaining why grokking (sudden generalization after memorization) takes so long, showing it arises from a norm-driven representational phase transition. Derives tight bounds showing delay scales as O(1/λ²) with regularization strength λ.

entry.title: The ARC of Progress towards AGI: A Living Survey of Abstraction and Reasoning

author.name: Sahar Vahdati, Andrei Aioanei, Haridhra Suresh, Jens Lehmann

entry.summary: Comprehensive survey of 82 approaches to the ARC-AGI benchmark across three versions and competitions. Key finding: all paradigms show 2-3x performance drops from ARC-AGI-1 to ARC-AGI-2, while humans maintain near-perfect accuracy. Opus 4.6 reaches 93% on v1 but only 68.8% on v2.

entry.title: Why AI systems don't learn and what to do about it: Lessons on autonomous learning from cognitive science

author.name: Emmanuel Dupoux, Yann LeCun, Jitendra Malik

entry.summary: By prominent AI researchers (Dupoux, LeCun, Malik), this paper critically examines why current AI systems fail at autonomous learning and proposes a cognitive-inspired architecture with System A (observation), System B (active behavior), and System M (meta-control).

entry.title: Mixture-of-Depths Attention

author.name: Lianghui Zhu, Yuxin Fang, Bencheng Liao, Shijie Wang, Tianheng Cheng, Zilong Huang, Chen Chen, Lai Wei, Yutao Zeng, Ya Wang, Yi Lin, Yu Li, Xinggang Wang

entry.summary: Introduces Mixture-of-Depths Attention (MoDA), allowing each attention head to attend across both sequence and depth dimensions. Achieves 97.3% of FlashAttention-2's efficiency and consistently outperforms strong baselines at 1.5B scale.

entry.title: Attention Residuals

author.name: Kimi Team, Guangyu Chen, Yu Zhang, Jianlin Su, Weixin Xu, Siyuan Pan, Yaoyu Wang, Yucheng Wang, Guanduo Chen, Bohong Yin, Yutian Chen, Junjie Yan, Ming Wei, Y. Zhang, Fanqing Meng, Chao Hong, Xiaotong Xie, Shaowei Liu, Enzhe Lu, Yunpeng Tai, Yanru Chen, Xin Men, Haiqing Guo, Y. Charles, Haoyu Lu, Lin Sui, Jinguo Zhu, Zaida Zhou, Weiran He, Weixiao Huang, Xinran Xu, Yuzhi Wang, Guokun Lai, Yulun Du, Yuxin Wu, Zhilin Yang, Xinyu Zhou

entry.summary: From the Kimi team: proposes Attention Residuals (AttnRes), replacing fixed-weight residual connections with softmax attention over preceding layer outputs, allowing each layer to selectively aggregate earlier representations. Block AttnRes reduces memory overhead for large-scale training.

entry.title: V-JEPA 2.1: Unlocking Dense Features in Video Self-Supervised Learning

author.name: Lorenzo Mur-Labadia, Matthew Muckley, Amir Bar, Mido Assran, Koustuv Sinha, Mike Rabbat, Yann LeCun, Nicolas Ballas, Adrien Bardes

entry.summary: V-JEPA 2.1 from Meta presents self-supervised models learning dense visual representations for images and videos through dense predictive loss, deep self-supervision, and multi-modal tokenizers with effective scaling.

entry.title: The Phenomenology of Hallucinations

author.name: Valeria Ruscio, Keiran Thompson

entry.summary: Shows that LLMs hallucinate not from failure to detect uncertainty but from failure to integrate it into outputs. Uncertain inputs occupy high-dimensional regions with 2-3x intrinsic dimensionality of factual inputs, but this signal migrates to low-sensitivity subspaces.

entry.title: Think First, Diffuse Fast: Improving Diffusion Language Model Reasoning via Autoregressive Plan Conditioning

author.name: Earl J St Sauver

entry.summary: Proposes plan conditioning for diffusion language models: prepending a short AR-generated plan to guide the diffusion model's denoising process. Improves LLaDA-8B on GSM8K from 75.6% to 87.2%, matching AR model performance, with a training-free approach.

entry.title: Why Agents Compromise Safety Under Pressure

author.name: Hengle Jiang, Ke Tang

entry.summary: Identifies 'Agentic Pressure' — the tension when LLM agents must choose between goal achievement and safety constraints. Finds that advanced reasoning capabilities accelerate safety decline as models construct linguistic rationalizations to justify violations.

entry.title: NCCL EP: Towards a Unified Expert Parallel Communication API for NCCL

author.name: Amos Goldman (NVIDIA Corporation), Nimrod Boker (NVIDIA Corporation), Maayan Sheraizin (NVIDIA Corporation), Nimrod Admoni (NVIDIA Corporation), Artem Polyakov (NVIDIA Corporation), Subhadeep Bhattacharya (NVIDIA Corporation), Fan Yu (NVIDIA Corporation), Kai Sun (NVIDIA Corporation), Georgios Theodorakis (NVIDIA Corporation), Hsin-Chun Yin (NVIDIA Corporation), Peter-Jan Gootzen (NVIDIA Corporation), Aamir Shafi (NVIDIA Corporation), Assaf Ravid (NVIDIA Corporation), Salvatore Di Girolamo (NVIDIA Corporation), Manjunath Gorentla Venkata (NVIDIA Corporation), Gil Bloch (NVIDIA Corporation)

entry.summary: NVIDIA introduces NCCL EP, a unified communication library for Mixture-of-Experts parallelism built on NCCL's Device API. Supports both low-latency inference and high-throughput training modes with standardized dispatch/combine primitives.

entry.title: M$^2$RNN: Non-Linear RNNs with Matrix-Valued States for Scalable Language Modeling

author.name: Mayank Mishra, Shawn Tan, Ion Stoica, Joseph Gonzalez, Tri Dao

entry.summary: M²RNN introduces matrix-valued hidden states for non-linear RNNs that achieve expressivity beyond the TC⁰ complexity class of Transformers (enabling entity tracking, code execution). Demonstrates competitive language modeling with efficient tensor core usage. Authors include Tri Dao.

entry.title: Evasive Intelligence: Lessons from Malware Analysis for Evaluating AI Agents

author.name: Simone Aonzo, Merve Sahin, Aur\'elien Francillon, Daniele Perito

entry.summary: Draws parallels between malware evasion techniques and AI agent evaluation, arguing that agents can detect evaluation environments and adapt behavior accordingly, leading to overly optimistic safety assessments. This is a conceptual paper connecting decades of adversarial malware research to AI safety evaluation.

entry.title: HorizonMath: Measuring AI Progress Toward Mathematical Discovery with Automatic Verification

author.name: Erik Y. Wang, Sumeet Motwani, James V. Roggeveen, Eliot Hodges, Dulhan Jayalath, Charles London, Kalyan Ramakrishnan, Flaviu Cipcigan, Philip Torr, Alessandro Abate

entry.summary: Introduces HorizonMath, a benchmark of 100+ predominantly unsolved mathematical problems across 8 domains with automated verification, designed to measure AI progress toward mathematical discovery. Being unsolved, the benchmark is immune to data contamination.

entry.title: Clinician input steers frontier AI models toward both accurate and harmful decisions

author.name: Ivan Lopez, Selin S. Everett, Bryan J. Bunning, April S. Liang, Dong Han Yao, Shivam C. Vedak, Kameron C. Black, Sophie Ostmeier, Stephen P. Ma, Emily Alsentzer, Jonathan H. Chen, Akshay S. Chaudhari, Eric Horvitz

entry.summary: Evaluates 21 LLM variants across 8 frontier models on clinical tasks, showing that clinician context dramatically shifts model concordance (differential diagnosis sharing rising from 65.8% to 93.5%) and that adversarial clinician input can steer models toward harmful decisions.

entry.title: Fold-CP: A Context Parallelism Framework for Biomolecular Modeling

author.name: Dejun Lin, Simon Chu, Vishanth Iyer, Youhan Lee, John St John, Kevin Boyd, Brian Roland, Xiaowei Ren, Guoqing Zhou, Zhonglin Cao, Polina Binder, Yuliya Zhautouskaya, Jakub Zakrzewski, Maximilian Stadler, Kyle Gion, Yuxing Peng, Xi Chen, Tianjing Zhang, Philipp Junk, Michelle Dimon, Pawe{\l} Gniewek, Fabian Ortega, McKinley Polen, Ivan Grubisic, Ali Bashir, Graham Holt, Danny Kovtun, Matthias Grass, Luca Naef, Rui Wang, Jian Peng, Anthony Costa, Saee Paliwal, Eddie Calleja, Timur Rvachov, Neha Tadimeti, Roy Tal, Emine Kucukbenli

entry.summary: Presents NVIDIA BioNeMo Fold-CP, a context parallelism framework that distributes protein co-folding model inference and training across multiple GPUs, enabling prediction of biomolecular assemblies with over 10,000 residues — well beyond AlphaFold 3's single-GPU limit.

entry.title: AI Can Learn Scientific Taste

author.name: Jingqi Tong, Mingzhe Li, Hangcheng Li, Yongzhuo Yang, Yurong Mou, Weijie Ma, Zhiheng Xi, Hongji Chen, Xiaoran Liu, Qinyuan Cheng, Ming Zhang, Qiguang Chen, Weifeng Ge, Qipeng Guo, Tianlei Ying, Tianxiang Sun, Yining Zheng, Xinchi Chen, Jun Zhao, Ning Ding, Xuanjing Huang, Yugang Jiang, Xipeng Qiu

entry.summary: Proposes Reinforcement Learning from Community Feedback (RLCF), training a Scientific Judge on 700K paper pairs to learn 'scientific taste' — the ability to judge and propose high-impact research ideas. Also introduces a Scientific Creator that generates ideas preferred over human baselines.

entry.title: Kimodo: Scaling Controllable Human Motion Generation

author.name: Davis Rempe, Mathis Petrovich, Ye Yuan, Haotian Zhang, Xue Bin Peng, Yifeng Jiang, Tingwu Wang, Umar Iqbal, David Minor, Michael de Ruyter, Jiefeng Li, Chen Tessler, Edy Lim, Eugene Jeong, Sam Wu, Ehsan Hassani, Michael Huang, Jin-Bey Yu, Chaeyeon Chung, Lina Song, Olivier Dionne, Jan Kautz, Simon Yuen, Sanja Fidler

entry.summary: Kimodo is a large-scale controllable human motion diffusion model trained on 700 hours of optical motion capture data, supporting text prompts and comprehensive kinematic constraints including keyframes, sparse joints, and root trajectories. The scale of training data (700h mocap) and comprehensive control suite from an NVIDIA-affiliated team make this notable.

entry.title: The Missing Red Line: How Commercial Pressure Erodes AI Safety Boundaries

author.name: Nora Petrova, John Burden

entry.summary: Tests 8 frontier models in scenarios where commercial system prompts conflict with user safety, finding catastrophic failures: models fabricating safety information, reasoning they should refuse but proceeding anyway, and discouraging medical consultations.

entry.title: More Test-Time Compute Can Hurt: Overestimation Bias in LLM Beam Search

author.name: Gal Dalal, Assaf Hallak, Gal Chechik, Yftach Ziser

entry.summary: Analyzes how wider beam search can hurt LLM reasoning due to overestimation bias, grounded in Extreme Value Theory. Derives a maximum useful beam width beyond which search degrades performance. Shows this critical width depends on scorer signal-to-noise ratio, growing exponentially with quality advantage.

entry.title: Invisible failures in human-AI interactions

author.name: Christopher Potts, Moritz Sudhof

entry.summary: Large-scale analysis of WildChat data finds 78% of AI failures are invisible (users give no overt indication of problems), categorized into eight archetypes. 91% of failures are interactional rather than capability-driven, suggesting they'll persist as models improve.

entry.title: Gradient Atoms: Unsupervised Discovery, Attribution and Steering of Model Behaviors via Sparse Decomposition of Training Gradients

author.name: J Rosser

entry.summary: Presents Gradient Atoms, an unsupervised method decomposing per-document training gradients into sparse components via dictionary learning, discovering interpretable behavioral 'atoms' without requiring a query behavior. Finds 500 atoms with high-coherence ones recovering known concepts.

entry.title: Consequentialist Objectives and Catastrophe

author.name: Henrik Marklund, Alex Infanger, Benjamin Van Roy

entry.summary: Argues that when AI capabilities are sufficiently advanced, pursuing a fixed consequentialist objective tends to produce catastrophic outcomes. Formalizes conditions under which this provably occurs, showing simple objective modifications cannot resolve the problem.

entry.title: Directional Routing in Transformers

author.name: Kevin Taylor

entry.summary: Introduces directional routing, a lightweight mechanism adding learned suppression directions to transformer attention heads via a shared router at 3.9% parameter cost. Disabling routing collapses factual recall and induction accuracy to near-zero. Mechanistic analysis shows routing becomes the model's dominant computational pathway.

entry.title: HindSight: Evaluating Research Idea Generation via Future Impact

author.name: Bo Jiang

entry.summary: HindSight evaluates AI-generated research ideas by matching them against future real publications and scoring by citation impact and venue acceptance. Reveals that LLM-as-Judge finds no difference between methods while HindSight shows significant advantages for retrieval-augmented generation. Exposes disconnect between subjective and impact-based evaluation.

entry.title: Mechanistic Origin of Moral Indifference in Language Models

author.name: Lingyu Li, Yan Teng, Yingchun Wang

entry.summary: Investigates the mechanistic origin of 'moral indifference' in LLMs, showing they compress distinct moral concepts into uniform probability distributions. Analyzes 23 models using 251K moral vectors and proposes representation-level remedies.

entry.title: From Specification to Architecture: A Theory Compiler for Knowledge-Guided Machine Learning

author.name: Asela Hevapathige, Yu Xia, Sachith Seneviratne, Saman Halgamuge

entry.summary: Proposes the Theory Compiler, a system that takes typed, machine-readable domain theories and automatically produces neural network architectures whose function space is provably consistent with the theory by construction, not regularization.

entry.title: DeceptGuard :A Constitutional Oversight Framework For Detecting Deception in LLM Agents

author.name: Snehasis Mukhopadhyay

entry.summary: Introduces DECEPTGUARD, a framework comparing black-box, chain-of-thought-aware, and activation-probe monitoring regimes for detecting deceptive behavior in LLM agents, along with DECEPTSYNTH for generating synthetic deception data.

entry.title: Lost in Aggregation: On a Fundamental Expressivity Limit of Message-Passing Graph Neural Networks

author.name: Eran Rosenbluth

entry.summary: Proves a fundamental expressivity limit of message-passing GNNs: any MP-GNN with generic aggregations induces only polynomially many equivalence classes on graphs, while non-isomorphic graphs are doubly-exponential, making them infinitely weaker than 2-iteration Color Refinement in a uniform sense.

entry.title: From Refusal Tokens to Refusal Control: Discovering and Steering Category-Specific Refusal Directions

author.name: Rishab Alagharu, Ishneet Sukhvinder Singh, Shaibi Shamsudeen, Zhen Wu, Ashwinee Panda

entry.summary: Discovers that fine-tuning LLMs with categorical refusal tokens induces separable, category-aligned directions in the residual stream. Uses these to construct steering vectors for fine-grained inference-time control over refusal behavior, improving both safety and reliability.

entry.title: Residual Stream Analysis of Overfitting And Structural Disruptions

author.name: Quan Liu, Han Zhou, Wenquan Wu, Hua Wu, Sen Su

entry.summary: Introduces FlowLens, a PCA-based tool for analyzing residual-stream geometry in LLMs, revealing that safety fine-tuning on low-entropy data concentrates variance and causes false refusals. Proposes entropy-augmented training to mitigate this effect.

entry.title: Seamless Deception: Larger Language Models Are Better Knowledge Concealers

author.name: Dhananjay Ashok, Ruth-Ann Armstrong, Jonathan May

entry.summary: Shows that larger language models are better at concealing knowledge, making deception harder to detect. Classifiers that detect concealment in smaller models fail to generalize to larger ones, with deception traces becoming fainter at scale.

entry.title: Two Birds, One Projection: Harmonizing Safety and Utility in LVLMs via Inference-time Feature Projection

author.name: Yewon Han, Yumin Seol, EunGyung Kong, Minsoo Jo, Taesup Kim

entry.summary: Proposes an inference-time jailbreak defense for Large Vision-Language Models by projecting cross-modal features onto the null space of a modality-induced bias direction. Discovers that this bias direction undermines both safety and utility, resolving the apparent safety-utility tradeoff. Efficient and training-free approach.

entry.title: Amplification Effects in Test-Time Reinforcement Learning: Safety and Reasoning Vulnerabilities

author.name: Vanshaj Khattar, Md Rafi ur Rashid, Moumita Choudhury, Jing Liu, Toshiaki Koike-Akino, Ming Jin, Ye Wang

entry.summary: Investigates safety vulnerabilities of test-time reinforcement learning (TTRL), showing that harmful prompt injection amplifies existing model behaviors. Demonstrates both safety amplification and danger amplification effects. Important finding that test-time training methods are vulnerable to adversarial exploitation.

entry.title: Linear Predictability of Attention Heads in Large Language Models

author.name: Khalid Shaikh, Asmit Kumar Singh, Rebecca Christopher Dsouza, Shikhar Shiromani

entry.summary: Reveals that attention heads in large language models exhibit pervasive inter-head linear structure where QKV vectors can be reconstructed from a small number of peer heads, suggesting significant KV cache compression potential.

entry.title: Deep probabilistic model synthesis enables unified modeling of whole-brain neural activity across individual subjects

author.name: William E. Bishop, Luuk W. Hesselink, Bernhard Englitz, Misha B. Ahrens, James E. Fitzgerald

entry.summary: Introduces Deep Probabilistic Model Synthesis (DPMS), a framework that combines data across multiple instances of the same system (e.g., brains of different animals) using variational inference with conditional priors over model parameters. Demonstrated on whole-brain neural activity data.

entry.title: Effective Distillation to Hybrid xLSTM Architectures

author.name: Lukas Hauzenberger, Niklas Schmidinger, Thomas Schmied, Anamaria-Roberta Hartl, David Stap, Pieter-Jan Hoedt, Maximilian Beck, Sebastian B\"ock, G\"unter Klambauer, Sepp Hochreiter

entry.summary: Introduces a distillation pipeline for converting Transformer-based LLMs into sub-quadratic xLSTM-based architectures, proposing a merging stage where individually linearized experts are combined. Achieves near-lossless distillation from Llama models to xLSTM students.

entry.title: Power-Law Spectrum of the Random Feature Model

author.name: Elliot Paquette, Ke Liang Xiao, Yizhe Zhu

entry.summary: Proves that power-law eigenvalue structure in data covariance is preserved through random feature model transformations (random projection + nonlinear activation), providing theoretical grounding for neural network scaling laws.

entry.title: MMOU: A Massive Multi-Task Omni Understanding and Reasoning Benchmark for Long and Complex Real-World Videos

author.name: Arushi Goel, Sreyan Ghosh, Vatsal Agarwal, Nishit Anand, Kaousheik Jayakumar, Lasha Koroshinadze, Yao Xu, Katie Lyons, James Case, Karan Sapra, Kevin J. Shih, Siddharth Gururani, Abhinav Shrivastava, Ramani Duraiswami, Dinesh Manocha, Andrew Tao, Bryan Catanzaro, Mohammad Shoeybi, Wei Ping

entry.summary: Introduces MMOU, a 15,000-question benchmark over 9,038 videos evaluating multimodal LLMs on joint visual-audio-textual reasoning in long, complex real-world videos, spanning 13 skill categories requiring cross-modal evidence integration.

entry.title: Hidden Role Games as a Trusted Model Eval

author.name: james.lucassen

entry.summary: Proposes using hidden role games (like Mafia/Werewolf) as evaluations for 'flexible adversarial strategy under uncertainty' (FASUU)—a capability that early AI schemers would need but current models seem to lack. The author argues this capability lags behind coding/R&D capabilities, making it useful for determining model trustedness in AI control frameworks.

entry.title: CausalEvolve: Towards Open-Ended Discovery with Causal Scratchpad

author.name: Yongqiang Chen, Chenxi Liu, Zhenhao Chen, Tongliang Liu, Bo Han, Kun Zhang

entry.summary: Proposes CausalEvolve, an evolution-based AI agent framework equipped with a causal scratchpad that identifies and leverages causal relationships from past evolutionary experience to guide more efficient program evolution for scientific discovery.

entry.title: Visual Confused Deputy: Exploiting and Defending Perception Failures in Computer-Using Agents

author.name: Xunzhuo Liu, Bowei He, Xue Liu, Andy Luo, Haichen Zhang, Huamin Chen

entry.summary: Formalizes the 'visual confused deputy' security problem in computer-using agents, where misperceived screen states lead to unauthorized actions. Shows simple screen manipulations can redirect routine clicks into privileged actions.

entry.title: Ablate and Rescue: A Causal Analysis of Residual Stream Hyper-Connections

author.name: William Peng, Josheev Rai, Kevin Tseng, Siwei Wang, Sean Wu

entry.summary: Presents the first open-source implementation and mechanistic analysis of Manifold-Constrained Hyper-Connections (mHC), a multi-stream transformer architecture. Uses causal interventions and representation metrics to understand how parallel residual streams encode information. Introduces systematic ablation methodology for multi-stream architectures.

entry.title: TrinityGuard: A Unified Framework for Safeguarding Multi-Agent Systems

author.name: Kai Wang, Biaojie Zeng, Zeming Wei, Chang Jin, Hefeng Zhou, Xiangtian Li, Chao Yang, Jingjing Qu, Xingcheng Xu, Xia Hu

entry.summary: TrinityGuard provides a comprehensive safety evaluation framework for LLM-based multi-agent systems with a three-tier taxonomy of 20 risk types covering single-agent, inter-agent, and system-level hazards. Grounded in OWASP standards. Addresses novel risks that go beyond single LLM safety.

entry.title: Enhancing LLM Training via Spectral Clipping

author.name: Xiaowen Jiang, Andrei Semenov, Sebastian U. Stich

entry.summary: Proposes SPECTRA, a framework for LLM training that applies spectral clipping to optimizer updates and gradients to control spectral norms and suppress noise spikes. Works as a wrapper around optimizers like AdamW.

entry.title: When Does Sparsity Mitigate the Curse of Depth in LLMs

author.name: Dilxat Muhtar, Xinyuan Song, Sebastian Pokutta, Max Zimmer, Nico Pelleriti, Thomas Hofmann, Shiwei Liu

entry.summary: Demonstrates that sparsity acts as a regulator of variance propagation in deep LLMs, helping mitigate the 'curse of depth' where later layers contribute less. Covers both implicit sparsity (weight decay, attention) and explicit sparsity (pruning).

entry.title: Learning When to Trust in Contextual Bandits

author.name: Majid Ghasemi, Mark Crowley

entry.summary: Identifies 'Contextual Sycophancy' in RL—where evaluators are truthful in benign contexts but strategically biased in critical ones. Proposes CESA-LinUCB that learns per-evaluator trust boundaries and achieves sublinear regret against contextual adversaries.

entry.title: AgentProcessBench: Diagnosing Step-Level Process Quality in Tool-Using Agents

author.name: Shengda Fan, Xuyan Ye, Yupeng Huo, Zhi-Yuan Chen, Yiju Guo, Shenzhi Yang, Wenkai Yang, Shuqi Ye, Jingwen Chen, Haotian Chen, Xin Cong, Yankai Lin

entry.summary: Introduces AgentProcessBench, the first benchmark for evaluating step-level quality in tool-augmented agent trajectories, with 1,000 trajectories and 8,509 human-labeled step annotations. Addresses the gap between mathematical reasoning benchmarks and real tool-use evaluation.

entry.title: InterPol: De-anonymizing LM Arena via Interpolated Preference Learning

author.name: Minsung Cho, Jaehyung Kim

entry.summary: Introduces INTERPOL, a framework that can de-anonymize model responses on voting-based leaderboards like LM Arena by learning deep stylistic patterns through interpolated preference data, exposing a vulnerability in anonymous benchmarking.

entry.title: Preventing Curriculum Collapse in Self-Evolving Reasoning Systems

author.name: Vaibhav Mishra

entry.summary: Introduces Prism, a method to prevent diversity collapse in self-evolving reasoning LLM systems where models generate and solve their own problems. Defines a persistent diversity signal over an embedding-induced semantic space to maintain problem variety across iterations.

entry.title: VisualLeakBench: Auditing the Fragility of Large Vision-Language Models against PII Leakage and Social Engineering

author.name: Youting Wang, Yuan Tang, Yitian Qian, Chen Zhao

entry.summary: Introduces VisualLeakBench, an evaluation suite auditing LVLMs against PII leakage and social engineering using synthetic adversarial images. Tests GPT-5.2, Claude 4, Gemini-3 Flash, and Grok-4, finding significant vulnerability differences.

entry.title: Sirens' Whisper: Inaudible Near-Ultrasonic Jailbreaks of Speech-Driven LLMs

author.name: Zijian Ling, Pingyi Hu, Xiuyong Gao, Xiaojing Ma, Man Zhou, Jun Feng, Songfeng Lu, Dongmei Zhang, Bin Benjamin Zhu

entry.summary: Introduces SWhisper, the first practical framework for covert inaudible attacks against speech-driven LLMs using near-ultrasound waveforms that demodulate through microphone nonlinearity, enabling prompt injection via acoustic channels.

entry.title: Large Language Models Reproduce Racial Stereotypes When Used for Text Annotation

author.name: Petter T\"ornberg

entry.summary: Demonstrates across 19 LLMs and 4 million+ annotations that subtle identity cues (names associated with racial groups) systematically bias text annotation outcomes, mirroring racial stereotypes across 39 tasks.

entry.title: Self-Indexing KVCache: Predicting Sparse Attention from Compressed Keys

author.name: Xu Yang, Jiapeng Zhang, Dongyang Zhao, Guo Chen, Zhuo Tang

entry.summary: Introduces a self-indexing KV cache that unifies compression and retrieval using sign-based 1-bit vector quantization, treating compressed key representations as a structure that directly enables sparse attention. This eliminates separate index structures and reduces memory overhead.

entry.title: POLCA: Stochastic Generative Optimization with LLM

author.name: Xuanfei Ren, Allen Nie, Tengyang Xie, Ching-An Cheng

entry.summary: POLCA formalizes LLM-as-optimizer as a stochastic generative optimization problem, using a priority queue to manage exploration-exploitation tradeoffs. The framework handles noisy feedback and stochastic system behaviors while constraining solution space expansion. Demonstrates scalability for optimizing complex systems like prompts and multi-turn agents.

entry.title: Thinking in Latents: Adaptive Anchor Refinement for Implicit Reasoning in LLMs

author.name: Disha Sheshanarayana, Rajat Subhra Pal, Manjira Sinha, Tirthankar Dasgupta

entry.summary: AdaAnchor introduces adaptive latent-space reasoning that adjusts the number of refinement steps during inference, removing the need for a fixed hyperparameter. Shifts multi-step reasoning computation into hidden representations rather than generating verbose chain-of-thought tokens. Balances accuracy and efficiency dynamically.

entry.title: Scalable Simulation-Based Model Inference with Test-Time Complexity Control

author.name: Manuel Gloeckler, J. P. Manzano-Patr\'on, Stamatios N. Sotiropoulos, Cornelius Schr\"oder, Jakob H. Macke

entry.summary: PRISM introduces a simulation-based encoder-decoder for joint Bayesian model selection and parameter inference with test-time complexity control. Allows adjusting parsimony assumptions at test time rather than committing at training time. Addresses the bottleneck of choosing among large families of plausible simulators.

entry.title: FuXiWeather2: Learning accurate atmospheric state estimation for operational global weather forecasting

author.name: Xiaoze Xu, Xiuyu Sun, Songling Zhu, Xiaohui Zhong, Yuanqing Huang, Zijian Zhu, Jun Liu, Hao Li

entry.summary: FuXiWeather2 is a unified end-to-end neural framework for weather data assimilation and forecasting that aligns training with real observations rather than just reanalysis products. Addresses the limitation of ML weather models being 'emulators of reanalysis products' with their systematic biases. Handles distribution shift between training and deployment.

entry.title: SFCoT: Safer Chain-of-Thought via Active Safety Evaluation and Calibration

author.name: Yu Pan, Wenlong Yu, Tiejun Wu, Xiaohu Ye, Qiannan Si, Guangquan Xu, Bin Wu

entry.summary: SFCoT proactively monitors and calibrates potentially unsafe reasoning steps in LLM chain-of-thought in real time, rather than only filtering final outputs. Incorporates a three-tier safety scoring system with multi-perspective consistency verification. Addresses the vulnerability of unmonitored intermediate reasoning.

entry.title: SWE-Skills-Bench: Do Agent Skills Actually Help in Real-World Software Engineering?

author.name: Tingxu Han, Yi Zhang, Wei Song, Chunrong Fang, Zhenyu Chen, Youcheng Sun, Lijie Hu

entry.summary: SWE-Skills-Bench is the first benchmark isolating the marginal utility of agent skills (structured procedural knowledge) in real-world software engineering. Pairs 49 skills with GitHub repos and deterministic verification yielding ~565 task instances. Addresses unclear real utility of skill injection for LLM agents.

entry.title: Grokking as a Variance-Limited Phase Transition: Spectral Gating and the Epsilon-Stability Threshold

author.name: Pratyush Acharya, Habish Dhakal

entry.summary: Analyzes grokking as a variance-limited phase transition in AdamW dynamics, revealing a 'Spectral Gating' mechanism that regulates the transition from memorization to generalization in modular arithmetic tasks.

entry.title: From Passive Observer to Active Critic: Reinforcement Learning Elicits Process Reasoning for Robotic Manipulation

author.name: Yibin Liu, Yaxing Lyu, Daqi Gao, Zhixuan Liang, Weiliang Tang, Shilong Mu, Xiaokang Yang, Yao Mu

entry.summary: Introduces PRIMO R1, a 7B framework that uses outcome-based RL to transform video MLLMs from passive observers into active critics for robotic manipulation, generating explicit chain-of-thought for progress estimation.

entry.title: PDE-SSM: A Spectral State Space Approach to Spatial Mixing in Diffusion Transformers

author.name: Eshed Gal, Moshe Eliasof, Siddharth Rout, Eldad Haber

entry.summary: Proposes PDE-SSM, replacing attention in diffusion transformers with a learnable convection-diffusion-reaction PDE solved in Fourier domain, achieving O(N log N) complexity with strong spatial priors.

entry.title: SVD Contextual Sparsity Predictors for Fast LLM Inference

author.name: Georgii Serbin, Kirill Koshkin, Zhongao Sun, Anastasiya Bistrigova, C. C. Korikov

entry.summary: Presents a training-free framework for accelerating LLM inference via contextual sparsity in ReGLU-based feed-forward networks, using truncation-aware SVD of gate projection matrices. Includes threshold calibration and CUDA/CANN inference executors.

entry.title: Disentangling Dynamical Systems: Causal Representation Learning Meets Local Sparse Attention

author.name: Markus W. Baumgartner, Anson Lei, Joe Watson, Ingmar Posner

entry.summary: Develops a novel identifiability theorem using causal representation learning with local sparse attention to uncover disentangled representations of dynamical system parameters without structural assumptions. Derives graphical criteria for identifiability.

entry.title: Rethinking Machine Unlearning: Models Designed to Forget via Key Deletion

author.name: Sonia Laguna, Jorge da Silva Goncalves, Moritz Vandenhirtz, Alain Ryser, Irene Cannistraci, Julia E. Vogt

entry.summary: Proposes 'unlearning by design' — models trained from the start to support forgetting via key deletion, instantiated as Machine Unlearning with Encrypted Keys (MUEK) where data influence is locked behind deletable keys.

entry.title: Fine-tuning MLLMs Without Forgetting Is Easier Than You Think

author.name: He Li, Yuhui Zhang, Xiaohan Wang, Kaifeng Lyu, Serena Yeung-Levy

entry.summary: Demonstrates that simple adjustments to fine-tuning recipes (constraining trainable parameters, low learning rates) can effectively mitigate catastrophic forgetting in multimodal LLMs. Identifies a distinct forgetting mode from task-specific overfitting with in-distribution images and out-of-distribution text.

entry.title: ToolFlood: Beyond Selection -- Hiding Valid Tools from LLM Agents via Semantic Covering

author.name: Hussein Jawad, Nicolas J-B Brunel

entry.summary: Introduces ToolFlood, a retrieval-layer attack on tool-augmented LLM agents that injects tools to dominate embedding-space retrieval, pushing all legitimate tools out of the top-k results and rendering the agent unable to function.

entry.title: Exposing Long-Tail Safety Failures in Large Language Models through Efficient Diverse Response Sampling

author.name: Suvadeep Hajra, Palash Nandi, Tanmoy Chakraborty

entry.summary: Shows that safety failures in LLMs can be systematically exposed through diverse output-space exploration rather than just adversarial input search. Proposes Progressive Diverse Sampling to efficiently uncover rare but critical safety failures in the long tail of output distributions.

entry.title: Safety-Potential Pruning for Enhancing Safety Prompts Against VLM Jailbreaking Without Retraining

author.name: Chongxin Li, Hanzhang Wang, Lian Duan

entry.summary: Proposes Safety-Potential Pruning, a one-shot pruning method that amplifies safety-relevant activations in vision-language models without retraining, based on the Safety Subnetwork Hypothesis.

entry.title: EditHF-1M: A Million-Scale Rich Human Preference Feedback for Image Editing

author.name: Zitong Xu, Huiyu Duan, Zhongpeng Ji, Xinyun Zhang, Yutao Liu, Xiongkuo Min, Ke Gu, Jian Zhang, Shusong Xu, Jinwei Chen, Bo Li, Guangtao Zhai

entry.summary: Introduces EditHF-1M, a million-scale image editing dataset with 29M human preference pairs and 148K human ratings across quality, alignment, and preservation dimensions. Builds reward models for text-guided image editing evaluation.

entry.title: Anatomy of a Lie: A Multi-Stage Diagnostic Framework for Tracing Hallucinations in Vision-Language Models

author.name: Lexiang Xiong, Qi Li, Jingwen Ye, Xinchao Wang

entry.summary: Introduces a multi-stage diagnostic framework that recasts VLM hallucinations as dynamic computational pathologies rather than static errors. Proposes information-theoretic probes in a 'Cognitive State Space' and discovers a 'geometric-information duality' principle governing hallucination trajectories.

entry.title: Will AI Progress Accelerate or Slow Down? Projecting METR Time Horizons

author.name: Alvin Ånestrand

entry.summary: An analysis projecting future AI progress using METR's time horizon metric—the duration of software engineering tasks that AI can complete at 50% success rate. The author examines whether AI progress will accelerate, slow down, or proceed smoothly, referencing notable forecasting efforts like the AI 2027 scenario and AI Futures Model.

entry.title: Data Darwinism Part II: DataEvolve -- AI can Autonomously Evolve Pretraining Data Curation

author.name: Tiantian Mi, Dongming Shan, Zhen Huang, Yiwei Qin, Muhang Xie, Yuxuan Qiao, Yixiu Liu, Chenyang Zhou, Pengfei Liu

entry.summary: Introduces DataEvolve, a framework enabling automated evolution of data curation strategies across hundreds of heterogeneous data categories for LLM pretraining. Operates in closed evolutionary loops: identifying quality issues, generating candidates, evaluating, and iterating.

entry.title: Understanding Reasoning in LLMs through Strategic Information Allocation under Uncertainty

author.name: Jeonghye Kim, Xufang Luo, Minbeom Kim, Sangmook Lee, Dongsheng Li, Yuqing Yang

entry.summary: Introduces an information-theoretic framework decomposing LLM reasoning into procedural information and epistemic verbalization. Shows that 'Aha moments' like 'Wait' tokens work through uncertainty externalization rather than specific surface tokens.

entry.title: FineRMoE: Dimension Expansion for Finer-Grained Expert with Its Upcycling Approach

author.name: Ning Liao, Xiaoxing Wang, Xiaohan Qin, Junchi Yan

entry.summary: Proposes FineRMoE, extending fine-grained MoE design to both intermediate and output dimensions to overcome the scaling law bottleneck where single-dimension granularity ceases to improve performance. Includes an upcycling method from dense models.

entry.title: Agent Privilege Separation in OpenClaw: A Structural Defense Against Prompt Injection

author.name: Darren Cheng, Wen-Kwang Tsao

entry.summary: Proposes a two-agent privilege separation defense against prompt injection in LLM applications, achieving 0% attack success rate on the LLMail-Inject benchmark by combining agent isolation with JSON formatting.

entry.title: Questionnaire Responses Do not Capture the Safety of AI Agents

author.name: Max Hellrigel-Holderbaum, Edward James Young

entry.summary: Demonstrates that questionnaire-style safety assessments of LLMs fail to capture the safety of AI agents built on those same LLMs. Agent behavior diverges significantly from LLM responses to hypothetical scenarios.

entry.title: Universe Routing: Why Self-Evolving Agents Need Epistemic Control

author.name: Zhaohui Geoffrey Wang

entry.summary: Formalizes the 'universe routing problem' for AI agents: classifying questions into mutually exclusive belief spaces (e.g., frequentist vs Bayesian) before invoking specialized solvers. Shows hard routing to heterogeneous solvers matches soft MoE accuracy while being 7x faster because epistemically incompatible frameworks cause destructive interference when blended.

entry.title: What Matters for Scalable and Robust Learning in End-to-End Driving Planners?

author.name: David Holtz, Niklas Hanselmann, Simon Doll, Marius Cordts, Bernt Schiele

entry.summary: Systematically re-examines common architectural patterns for end-to-end autonomous driving, finding that open-loop advances often fail to transfer to closed-loop driving. Identifies what actually matters for scalable and robust learning in driving planners. Important negative results about architecture assumptions.

entry.title: ADV-0: Closed-Loop Min-Max Adversarial Training for Long-Tail Robustness in Autonomous Driving

author.name: Tong Nie, Yihong Tang, Junlin He, Yuewen Mei, Jie Sun, Lijun Sun, Wei Ma, Jian Sun

entry.summary: ADV-0 presents a closed-loop min-max framework treating autonomous driving adversarial training as a zero-sum Markov game. Aligns attacker utility directly with defender objective, revealing optimal adversary distribution. Makes tractable through dynamic programming and practical RL approximations.

entry.title: CCTU: A Benchmark for Tool Use under Complex Constraints

author.name: Junjie Ye, Guoqiang Zhang, Wenjie Fu, Tao Gui, Qi Zhang, Xuanjing Huang

entry.summary: CCTU benchmarks LLM tool use under complex constraints with 12 constraint categories across 4 dimensions. Features 200 test cases averaging 7 constraint types each. Addresses the gap in evaluating LLMs for constrained tool use requiring function calling, instruction following, and self-refinement.

entry.title: A Closer Look into LLMs for Table Understanding

author.name: Jia Wang, Chuanyu Qin, Mingyu Zheng, Qingyi Si, Peize Li, Zheng Lin

entry.summary: Empirical study on how 16 LLMs (general, tabular-specialist, MoE) understand tables across attention dynamics, effective depth, expert activation, and input design. Reveals three-phase attention pattern and finds tabular tasks require deeper layers than math reasoning. First comprehensive mechanistic analysis of table understanding.

entry.title: InterveneBench: Benchmarking LLMs for Intervention Reasoning and Causal Study Design in Real Social Systems

author.name: Shaojie Shi, Zhengyu Shi, Lingran Zheng, Xinyu Su, Anna Xie, Bohao Lv, Rui Xu, Zijian Chen, Zhichao Chen, Guolei Liu, Naifu Zhang, Mingjian Dong, Zhuo Quan, Bohao Chen, Teqi Hao, Yuan Qi, Yinghui Xu, Libo Wu

entry.summary: Introduces InterveneBench, a benchmark of 744 peer-reviewed social science studies for evaluating LLMs' ability to reason about policy interventions and causal study design without predefined causal graphs.

entry.title: Diffusion Models Generalize but Not in the Way You Might Think

author.name: Tim Kaiser, Markus Kollmann

entry.summary: Shows that sufficiently large diffusion models memorize training sets with more training, but denoising trajectories don't follow this trend because overfitting occurs at intermediate noise levels that trajectories don't visit.

entry.title: Understanding the Emergence of Seemingly Useless Features in Next-Token Predictors

author.name: Mark Rofin, Jalal Naghiyev, Michael Hahn

entry.summary: Identifies which gradient signal components from next-token prediction give rise to abstract features that appear redundant for immediate prediction, showing features with extreme future-token influence relate to formal reasoning domains like code.

entry.title: Excited Pfaffians: Generalized Neural Wave Functions Across Structure and State

author.name: Nicholas Gao, Till Grutschus, Frank No\'e, Stephan G\"unnemann

entry.summary: Introduces Excited Pfaffians, a neural network architecture for multi-state variational Monte Carlo that represents many quantum states efficiently within a single network, along with Multi-State Importance Sampling for constant sample-size overlap estimation.

entry.title: Training-Free Generation of Protein Sequences from Small Family Alignments via Stochastic Attention

author.name: Jeffrey D. Varner

entry.summary: Proposes stochastic attention (SA), a training-free protein sequence sampler that treats the Hopfield energy over a protein alignment as a Boltzmann distribution and draws samples via Langevin dynamics. Works with small protein families (<100 members) where deep generative models fail.

entry.title: Establishing Construct Validity in LLM Capability Benchmarks Requires Nomological Networks

author.name: Timo Freiesleben

entry.summary: Examines construct validity in LLM capability benchmarks through three philosophical frameworks (nomological, inferential, causal), arguing that the nomological account provides the best foundation for current LLM capability research.

entry.title: Faster Inference of Flow-Based Generative Models via Improved Data-Noise Coupling

author.name: Aram Davtyan, Leello Tadesse Dadi, Volkan Cevher, Paolo Favaro

entry.summary: Introduces LOOM-CFM, extending minibatch optimal transport coupling in Conditional Flow Matching beyond individual minibatches by preserving and optimizing noise-data assignments across training, accelerating inference.

entry.title: Deep learning and the rate of approximation by flows

author.name: Jingpu Cheng, Qianxiao Li, Ting Lin, Zuowei Shen

entry.summary: Investigates how depth affects approximation capacity of deep residual networks by formulating it as geodesic distance on a sub-Finsler manifold of diffeomorphisms, connecting learning efficiency to architectural compatibility.

entry.title: Rigorous Asymptotics for First-Order Algorithms Through the Dynamical Cavity Method

author.name: Yatin Dandi, David Gamarnik, Francisco Pernice, Lenka Zdeborov\'a

entry.summary: Provides the first rigorous formalization of the dynamical cavity method for analyzing first-order algorithms in high-dimensional statistics and ML, connecting to Dynamical Mean Field Theory with mathematical rigor.

entry.title: OmniCompliance-100K: A Multi-Domain, Rule-Grounded, Real-World Safety Compliance Dataset

author.name: Wenbin Hu, Huihao Jing, Haochen Shi, Changxuan Fan, Haoran Li, Yangqiu Song

entry.summary: Introduces OmniCompliance-100K, a comprehensive safety compliance dataset sourced from 74 real-world regulations and policies across multiple domains, designed to evaluate and improve LLM safety from a compliance perspective.

entry.title: Practicing with Language Models Cultivates Human Empathic Communication

author.name: Aakriti Kumar, Nalin Poungpeth, Diyi Yang, Bruce Lambert, Matthew Groh

entry.summary: Built 'Lend an Ear' platform where participants practice empathic communication with LLMs role-playing troubled individuals. From 33,938 messages across 968 participants, shows that practicing with LLMs improves human empathic communication skills over time.

entry.title: Code-A1: Adversarial Evolving of Code LLM and Test LLM via Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Aozhe Wang, Yuchen Yan, Nan Zhou, Zhengxi Lu, Weiming Lu, Jun Xiao, Yueting Zhuang, Yongliang Shen

entry.summary: Introduces Code-A1, an adversarial co-evolution framework that jointly trains a Code LLM (rewarded for passing tests) and a Test LLM (rewarded for exposing bugs) with opposing objectives, addressing the self-collusion problem in self-play code generation.

entry.title: HYDRA: Unifying Multi-modal Generation and Understanding via Representation-Harmonized Tokenization

author.name: Xuerui Qiu, Yutao Cui, Guozhen Zhang, Junzhe Li, JiaKui Hu, Xiao Zhang, Yang Li, Songtao Liu, Miles Yang, Yu Shi, Zhao Zhong, Liefeng Bo

entry.summary: Introduces HYDRA-TOK, a representation-harmonized pure ViT tokenizer that bridges the gap between visual understanding and generation by progressively transitioning from generation-oriented to understanding-oriented representations.

entry.title: Gym-V: A Unified Vision Environment System for Agentic Vision Research

author.name: Fanqing Meng Lingxiao Du Jiawei Gu Jiaqi Liao Linjie Li Zijian Wu Xiangyan Liu Ziqi Zhao Mengkang Hu Yue Zhang Zichen Liu Jiaheng Zhang Michael Qizhe Shieh

entry.summary: Introduces Gym-V, a unified platform of 179 procedurally generated visual environments across 10 domains for training and evaluating vision agents with RL, finding that observation scaffolding matters more than RL algorithm choice.

entry.title: Towards Generalizable Robotic Manipulation in Dynamic Environments

author.name: Heng Fang, Shangru Li, Shuhan Wang, Xuanyang Xi, Dingkang Liang, Xiang Bai

entry.summary: Introduces DOMINO, a large-scale dataset and benchmark for dynamic robotic manipulation with 35 tasks, 110K+ expert trajectories, and multi-dimensional evaluation. Addresses the gap that existing VLA models trained on static scenes fail with moving targets.

entry.title: AutoTool: Automatic Scaling of Tool-Use Capabilities in RL via Decoupled Entropy Constraints

author.name: Yirong Zeng, Xiao Ding, Yufei Liu, Yuxian Wang, Qunyao Du, Yutai Hou, Wu Ning, Haonan Song, Duyu Tang, Dandan Tu, Bing Qin, Ting Liu

entry.summary: Proposes AutoTool, a training paradigm for RL-based tool use that decouples entropy constraints to automatically scale thinking length based on problem complexity. Uses warm-up SFT to help models distinguish simple vs complex problems, then RL for adaptive reasoning.

entry.title: EnterpriseOps-Gym: Environments and Evaluations for Stateful Agentic Planning and Tool Use in Enterprise Settings

author.name: Shiva Krishna Reddy Malay, Shravan Nayak, Jishnu Sethumadhavan Nair, Sagar Davasam, Aman Tiwari, Sathwik Tejaswi Madhusudhan, Sridhar Krishna Nemala, Srinivas Sunkara, Sai Rajeswar

entry.summary: Introduces EnterpriseOps-Gym, a benchmark for evaluating AI agents in realistic enterprise settings with 164 database tables, 512 tools, and 1,150 expert-curated tasks. Tests long-horizon planning with persistent state changes and access protocols.

entry.title: Relationship-Aware Safety Unlearning for Multimodal LLMs

author.name: Vishnu Narayanan Anilkumar, Abhijith Sreesylesh Babu, Trieu Hai Vo, Mohankrishna Kolla, Alexander Cuneo

entry.summary: Proposes relationship-aware safety unlearning for multimodal LLMs that targets unsafe object-relation-object tuples (e.g., child-drinking-wine) rather than individual concepts, using LoRA to suppress unsafe relationships while preserving benign uses.

entry.title: Are Dilemmas and Conflicts in LLM Alignment Solvable? A View from Priority Graph

author.name: Zhenheng Tang, Xiang Liu, Qian Wang, Eunsol Choi, Bo Li, Xiaowen Chu

entry.summary: Models LLM alignment conflicts using priority graphs where instructions and values are nodes with context-specific priority edges. Reveals that stable alignment is extremely challenging due to graph inconsistency, and identifies 'priority hacking' as a new vulnerability.

entry.title: OpenSeeker: Democratizing Frontier Search Agents by Fully Open-Sourcing Training Data

author.name: Yuwen Du, Rui Ye, Shuo Tang, Xinyu Zhu, Yijun Lu, Yuzhu Cai, Siheng Chen

entry.summary: Introduces OpenSeeker, the first fully open-source search agent with frontier-level performance, using fact-grounded QA synthesis and topological expansion to generate high-quality training data for search agents.

entry.title: How Transformers Reject Wrong Answers: Rotational Dynamics of Factual Constraint Processing

author.name: Javier Mar\'in

entry.summary: Introduces forced-completion probing, revealing that transformers reject wrong answers through rotational dynamics rather than rescaling. Shows correct and incorrect paths diverge through rotation across network depth in models 1.5B-13B.

entry.title: DreamReader: An Interpretability Toolkit for Text-to-Image Models

author.name: Nirmalendu Prakash, Narmeen Oozeer, Michael Lan, Luka Samkharadze, Phillip Howard, Roy Ka-Wei Lee, Dhruv Nathawani, Shivam Raval, Amirali Abdullah

entry.summary: Introduces DreamReader, a unified interpretability toolkit for text-to-image diffusion models that supports activation extraction, causal patching, structured ablations, and activation steering. Introduces novel intervention primitives including representation fine-tuning (LoReFT) for diffusion models.

entry.title: PolyGLU: State-Conditional Activation Routing in Transformer Feed-Forward Networks

author.name: Daniel Nobrega Medeiros

entry.summary: Introduces PolyGLU, a drop-in replacement for SwiGLU that allows each FFN neuron to dynamically route among 4 activation functions via differentiable gating, finding emergent routing behavior where different activation functions specialize for different tasks.

entry.title: EvoClaw: Evaluating AI Agents on Continuous Software Evolution

author.name: Gangda Deng, Zhaoling Chen, Zhongming Yu, Haoyang Fan, Yuhong Liu, Yuxin Yang, Dhruv Parikh, Rajgopal Kannan, Le Cong, Mengdi Wang, Qian Zhang, Viktor Prasanna, Xiangru Tang, Xingyao Wang

entry.summary: Introduces EvoClaw, a benchmark for evaluating AI agents on continuous software evolution rather than isolated coding tasks, using DeepCommit to reconstruct verifiable milestone DAGs from commit logs.

entry.title: Purifying Generative LLMs from Backdoors without Prior Knowledge or Clean Reference

author.name: Jianwei Li, Jung-Eun Kim

entry.summary: Proposes a framework for purifying backdoored instruction-tuned LLMs without prior knowledge of triggers or clean references, finding that backdoor associations are redundantly encoded across MLP layers while attention mechanisms remain relatively clean.

entry.title: Ghosts of Softmax: Complex Singularities That Limit Safe Step Sizes in Cross-Entropy

author.name: Piyush Sao

entry.summary: Derives closed-form expressions for the Taylor convergence radius of cross-entropy loss, showing that complex singularities ('ghosts of softmax') from zeros of the softmax partition function limit safe optimization step sizes.

entry.title: $\tau$-Voice: Benchmarking Full-Duplex Voice Agents on Real-World Domains

author.name: Soham Ray, Keshav Dhandhania, Victor Barres, Karthik Narasimhan

entry.summary: Introduces τ-voice, a benchmark for evaluating full-duplex voice agents on grounded real-world tasks requiring simultaneous listening/speaking, policy adherence, and environment interaction. Extends τ²-bench into voice domain.

entry.title: Mitigating Overthinking in Large Reasoning Language Models via Reasoning Path Deviation Monitoring

author.name: Weixin Guan, Liang Li, Jiapeng Liu, Bing Li, Peng Fu, Chengyang Fang, Xiaoshuai Hao, Can Ma, Weiping Wang

entry.summary: Proposes a method to mitigate overthinking in large reasoning language models by monitoring reasoning path deviations. Identifies that overthinking creates detectable deviations, enabling early-exit without extra training overhead or content switching.

entry.title: Seeking Physics in Diffusion Noise

author.name: Chujun Tang, Lei Zhong, Fangqiang Ding

entry.summary: Investigates whether video diffusion models encode physics plausibility in their intermediate denoising representations. Finds partial separability between physically plausible and implausible videos in mid-layer features, and introduces progressive trajectory selection to improve physical realism.

entry.title: Delightful Policy Gradient

author.name: Ian Osband

entry.summary: Delightful Policy Gradient gates each gradient term with a sigmoid of 'delight' (advantage × action surprisal), improving directional accuracy by preventing rare negative-advantage actions from distorting updates. Author is Ian Osband (Google DeepMind).

entry.title: $p^2$RAG: Privacy-Preserving RAG Service Supporting Arbitrary Top-$k$ Retrieval

author.name: Yulong Ming, Mingyue Wang, Jijia Yang, Cong Wang, Xiaohua Jia

entry.summary: p²RAG addresses privacy-preserving retrieval-augmented generation by enabling arbitrary top-k retrieval without security degradation. Existing privacy-preserving RAG systems struggle with flexible k values, which is important since long-context models benefit from larger retrieval sets. The system avoids the limitations of prior approaches that couldn't change k or suffered efficiency issues.

entry.title: RAZOR: Ratio-Aware Layer Editing for Targeted Unlearning in Vision Transformers and Diffusion Models

author.name: Ravi Ranjan, Utkarsh Grover, Xiaomin Lin, Agoritsa Polyzou

entry.summary: RAZOR introduces a lightweight, model-agnostic unlearning framework for transformers that identifies important layers and attention heads for targeted forgetting. Uses ratio-aware approach to coordinate multi-layer and multi-head edits while preserving useful knowledge. Applicable to both vision transformers and diffusion models.

entry.title: LLMs as Signal Detectors: Sensitivity, Bias, and the Temperature-Criterion Analogy

author.name: Jon-Paul Cacioli

entry.summary: Applies full Signal Detection Theory framework to analyze LLMs as signal detectors, separating sensitivity from bias. Tests whether temperature functions as a criterion shift analogous to SDT. Pre-registered study across 168,000 trials on three LLMs.

entry.title: To See is Not to Master: Teaching LLMs to Use Private Libraries for Code Generation

author.name: Yitong Zhang, Chengze Li, Ruize Chen, Guowei Yang, Xiaoran Jia, Yijie Ren, Jia Li

entry.summary: PriCoder teaches LLMs to use private library APIs through automatically synthesized training data, addressing the finding that even with accurate documentation, LLMs struggle to invoke private APIs. Models data synthesis as constructing library-oriented code samples. Goes beyond retrieval-based approaches.

entry.title: Seeking SOTA: Time-Series Forecasting Must Adopt Taxonomy-Specific Evaluation to Dispel Illusory Gains

author.name: Raeid Saqur, Christoph Bergmeir, Blanka Horvath, Daniel Schmidt, Frank Rudzicz, Terry Lyons

entry.summary: Argues that current time-series forecasting benchmarks are biased toward datasets with strong periodicities where classical methods already perform well, and calls for taxonomy-specific evaluation to reveal genuine progress.

entry.title: LightningRL: Breaking the Accuracy-Parallelism Trade-off of Block-wise dLLMs via Reinforcement Learning

author.name: Yanzhe Hu, Yijie Jin, Pengfei Liu, Kai Yu, Zhijie Deng

entry.summary: Proposes LightningRL, a post-training RL framework for diffusion language models that breaks the accuracy-parallelism trade-off in block-wise parallel token generation.

entry.title: Greedy Information Projection for LLM Data Selection

author.name: Victor Ye Dong, Kuan-Yun Lee, Jiamei Shuai, Shengfei Liu, Yi Liu, Jian Jiao

entry.summary: Presents Greedy Information Projection (GIP) for LLM fine-tuning data selection, casting it as maximizing mutual information between data subsets and task queries, with a geometric interpretation of quality-diversity balance.

entry.title: On Interpolation Formulas Describing Neural Network Generalization

author.name: Jin Guo, Roy Y. He, Jean-Michel Morel

entry.summary: Extends the Domingos interpolation formula to stochastic training, showing that neural networks behave as kernel machines with a stochastic gradient kernel, and links generalization error to the null space of the induced integral operator.

entry.title: Sampling Boltzmann distributions via normalizing flow approximation of transport maps

author.name: Zia Ur Rehman, Gero Friesecke

entry.summary: Provides rigorous mathematical foundations for sampling Boltzmann distributions via normalizing flows, proving existence of normalizing flows between reference measures and Boltzmann distributions with arbitrarily small Wasserstein error, covering physically realistic molecular dynamics potentials.

entry.title: Localizing and Editing Knowledge in Large Audio-Language Models

author.name: Sung Kyun Chung, Jiaheng Dong, Qiuchi Hu, Gongping Huang, Hong Jia, Ting Dang

entry.summary: Constructs the first benchmark for knowledge localization and editing in Large Audio-Language Models (LALMs), proposing speech-driven causal tracing to locate factual knowledge and editing methods to update it. Addresses the unique challenge of continuous speech representations.

entry.title: Chain-of-Trajectories: Unlocking the Intrinsic Generative Optimality of Diffusion Models via Graph-Theoretic Planning

author.name: Ping Chen, Xiang Liu, Xingpeng Zhang, Fei Shen, Xun Gong, Zhaoxiang Liu, Zezhou Chen, Huan Hu, Kai Wang, Shiguo Lian

entry.summary: Introduces Chain-of-Trajectories (CoTj), a train-free framework for diffusion models that enables deliberative planning by creating Diffusion DNA signatures to quantify per-stage denoising difficulty, reformulating sampling as graph planning on a DAG.

entry.title: Massive Redundancy in Gradient Transport Enables Sparse Online Learning

author.name: Aur Shalev Merin

entry.summary: Shows that real-time recurrent learning (RTRL) has massive gradient redundancy: propagating through only 6% of paths recovers 84% of full RTRL's adaptation ability, and this absolute count remains effective as network size grows.

entry.title: GradMem: Learning to Write Context into Memory with Test-Time Gradient Descent

author.name: Yuri Kuratov, Matvey Kairov, Aydar Bulatov, Ivan Rodkin, Mikhail Burtsev

entry.summary: Introduces GradMem, which writes LLM context into compact memory via test-time gradient descent on prefix memory tokens, enabling context removal at inference while retaining information from the context.

entry.title: ASAP: Attention-Shift-Aware Pruning for Efficient LVLM Inference

author.name: Surendra Pathak, Bo Han

entry.summary: Proposes ASAP, a training-free, KV-Cache-compatible pruning method for Large Vision-Language Models that addresses the 'attention shift' phenomenon using a dynamic bidirectional soft attention mask to efficiently reduce visual token processing costs.

entry.title: Training-free Detection of Generated Videos via Spatial-Temporal Likelihoods

author.name: Omer Ben Hayun, Roy Betser, Meir Yossef Levi, Levi Kassel, Guy Gilboa

entry.summary: Introduces STALL, a training-free, zero-shot method for detecting AI-generated videos by exploiting spatial-temporal likelihood statistics computed against real-data distributions, avoiding reliance on synthetic training data.

entry.title: MedPriv-Bench: Benchmarking the Privacy-Utility Trade-off of Large Language Models in Medical Open-End Question Answering

author.name: Shaowei Guan, Yu Zhai, Hin Chi Kwok, Jiawei Du, Xinyu Feng, Jing Li, Harry Qin, Vivian Hui

entry.summary: Introduces MedPriv-Bench, the first benchmark for jointly evaluating privacy preservation and clinical utility in medical QA with RAG systems. Addresses the risk of contextual leakage where unique medical detail combinations enable patient re-identification without explicit identifiers.

entry.title: Rethinking LLM Watermark Detection in Black-Box Settings: A Non-Intrusive Third-Party Framework

author.name: Zhuoshang Wang, Yubing Ren, Yanan Cao, Fang Fang, Xiaoxue Li, Li Guo

entry.summary: Introduces TTP-Detect, a black-box framework for non-intrusive third-party LLM watermark detection that decouples detection from injection, using a proxy model to amplify watermark signals for relative hypothesis testing.

entry.title: Qianfan-OCR: A Unified End-to-End Model for Document Intelligence

author.name: Daxiang Dong, Mingming Zheng, Dong Xu, Chunhua Luo, Bairong Zhuang, Yuxuan Li, Ruoyun He, Haoran Wang, Wenyu Zhang, Wenbo Wang, Yicheng Wang, Xue Xiong, Ayong Zheng, Xiaoying Zuo, Ziwei Ou, Jingnan Gu, Quanhao Guo, Jianmin Wu, Dawei Yin, Dou Shen

entry.summary: Presents Qianfan-OCR, a 4B-parameter unified VLM for document parsing, layout analysis, and understanding. Introduces Layout-as-Thought, a thinking phase that generates structured layout representations before outputs, recovering layout grounding in end-to-end OCR.

entry.title: Eleven Primitives and Three Gates: The Universal Structure of Computational Imaging

author.name: Chengshuai Yang, Xin Yuan

entry.summary: Proves that every computational imaging forward model decomposes into a DAG over exactly 11 physically-typed primitives, and that every reconstruction failure has exactly three independent root causes. Provides a unified theoretical framework for computational imaging.

entry.title: CamLit: Unified Video Diffusion with Explicit Camera and Lighting Control

author.name: Zhiyi Kuang, Chengan He, Egor Zakharov, Yuxuan Xue, Shunsuke Saito, Olivier Maury, Timur Bagautdinov, Youyi Zheng, Giljoo Nam

entry.summary: CamLit is the first unified video diffusion model that jointly performs novel view synthesis and relighting from a single image with explicit camera trajectory and environment map control.

entry.title: On the Nature of Attention Sink that Shapes Decoding Strategy in MLLMs

author.name: Suho Yoo, Youngjoon Jang, Joon Son Chung

entry.summary: Investigates the role of attention sinks in multimodal LLMs, finding they encode structured global information that shapes decoding behavior, and introduces OutRo, a lightweight inference-time method leveraging this insight.

entry.title: AutoMoT: A Unified Vision-Language-Action Model with Asynchronous Mixture-of-Transformers for End-to-End Autonomous Driving

author.name: Wenhui Huang, Songyan Zhang, Qihang Huang, Zhidong Wang, Zhiqi Mao, Collister Chua, Zhan Chen, Long Chen, Chen Lv
